issues.body:
### Check for previous/existing GitHub issues

- [x] I have checked for previous/existing GitHub issues

### Issue Type?

Feature Request

### Module Name

avm/res/storage/storage-account

### (Optional) Module Version

0.33.1

### Description

The module always calls `listKeys()` in its outputs, even when the caller sets `allowSharedKeyAccess: false`:

- `primaryAccessKey` and `secondaryAccessKey` (main.bicep lines 829 and 833)
- `primaryConnectionString` and `secondaryConnectionString` (lines 837 and 841)

Because outputs are always evaluated, every deployment reads the account keys. Two effects for a keyless setup:

1. The deploying identity must hold `Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/listkeys/action`, even though the account does not accept keys. A least-privilege deployer without it cannot use the module.
2. The keys land in the deployment's secure outputs, readable by anyone who can list them, when the intent was that no key ever leaves the account.

Request: make these outputs conditional on shared key access, the way `cognitive-services/account` already does (`output primaryKey string? = !disableLocalAuth ? cognitiveService.listKeys().key1 : null`) and `search/search-service` does for its admin keys. For example:

```bicep
output primaryAccessKey string? = allowSharedKeyAccess ? storageAccount.listKeys().keys[0].value : null
```

The `secretsExportConfiguration` path already runs only when asked, so it needs no change.

Today we keep a hand-written `Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts` resource instead of the module for this reason alone, and would move to the module once the outputs are conditional.

### Check for previous/existing GitHub issues

- [x] I have checked for previous/existing GitHub issues

### Issue Type?

Bug

### Module Name

avm/res/storage/storage-account

### (Optional) Module Version

0.33.1

### Description

When deploying an Azure Files share using the Storage Account AVM, the module attempts to set the accessTier property on the file share.

This causes a deployment/validation error when using a storage configuration where accessTier is not applicable/supported, in our case an Azure Files share used for FSLogix profile storage.

Current workaround: deploy the storage account using the AVM, but create the file service/share separately using the native Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/fileServices/shares Bicep resource without specifying accessTier.

It would be useful if accessTier could be optional and omitted from the generated file share resource when it is not explicitly configured or is not supported by the selected storage configuration.

This would allow the complete Azure Files configuration to remain within the AVM rather than requiring a mix of AVM and native Bicep resources.

A file share should be deployable through the Storage Account AVM without accessTier being set when no access tier has been specified by the caller.

### (Optional) Correlation Id

_No response_

issues.author: Miteshc1
issues.body:
### Check for previous/existing GitHub issues

- [x] I have checked for previous/existing GitHub issues

### Description

Feature request: Support Azure Files directory/file ACL configuration

When deploying Azure Files using the Storage Account AVM, we can create the storage account and file share and configure the required Azure RBAC permissions, but there is currently no way to configure the file-system ACLs required by workloads such as FSLogix as part of the deployment.

In our AVD deployment, the FSLogix profile share requires specific NTFS-style permissions for users/groups. We currently have to configure these separately after deployment using PowerShell 7 and Azure Files authentication.

It would be useful if the Storage Account AVM, or an associated AVM module/pattern, provided a supported mechanism for applying directory/file ACLs to an Azure Files share after creation.

This would allow Azure Files deployments, particularly common scenarios such as FSLogix profile storage, to be fully automated rather than requiring a separate post-deployment PowerShell step.

If this cannot be implemented directly within ARM/Bicep because the ACL configuration is a data-plane operation, an AVM-supported deployment pattern or extension for handling this would also be very useful.
issues.title: [AVM Question/Feedback]: Azure Files ACL configuration for FSLogix

### Issue Type?

Feature Request

### Module Name

avm/res/desktop-virtualization/host-pool

### (Optional) Module Version

0.8.2

### Description

Feature request: Support AVD Scheduled Agent Updates

The underlying Azure Virtual Desktop Host Pool resource supports the agentUpdate configuration for Scheduled Agent Updates, but this configuration is not currently exposed through the Host Pool AVM.

We would like to configure the agent update schedule declaratively as part of our AVD deployment, for example:

agentUpdate: {
  type: 'Scheduled'
  useSessionHostLocalTime: true
  maintenanceWindows: [
    {
      dayOfWeek: 'Sunday'
      hour: 3
    }
  ]
}

Currently this requires a separate post-deployment configuration step against the host pool.

It would be useful if the Host Pool AVM provided a supported mechanism for configuring agentUpdate, allowing the maintenance schedule to be managed declaratively alongside the rest of the AVD host pool configuration.

This would remove an additional post-deployment step and make the AVD deployment fully repeatable through Bicep.

### (Optional) Correlation Id

_No response_

We've just activated automatic checks for the [changelog spec BCPNFR22](https://azure.github.io/Azure-Verified-Modules/spec/BCPNFR22/). Please update your branch and add an entry to the CHANGELOG.md.

Sample entry for the `CHANGELOG.md` in the module directory is:

```text
## 0.2.1

### Changes

- Updated the referenced AVM common types

### Breaking Changes

- None
```

> The new version is calculated automatically, and you must set the new version in the changelog manually. The static tests will show you the expected version if you set it to something else.

[SNFR17 - Category: Release - Semantic Versioning](https://azure.github.io/Azure-Verified-Modules/spec/SNFR17/)

With a new minor version in the `version.json`, add **0** as patch. If you didn't change the version, the patch will be **patch+1**.

We are happy to help should you encounter a problem.

prs.body:
Adds support for configuring service endpoints on subnets within the sub-vending module. This change enables the definition and deployment of service endpoints, enhancing network security and connectivity options for resources within the subnet.

Fixes #6483

## Description
added line 
``` bicep
 serviceEndpoints: subnet.?serviceEndpoints
```

``` bicep
 subnets: [
      for (subnet, i) in virtualNetworkSubnets: (!empty(virtualNetworkSubnets))
        ? {
            name: subnet.name
            addressPrefix: subnet.?addressPrefix
            ipamPoolPrefixAllocations: subnet.?ipamPoolPrefixAllocations
            networkSecurityGroupResourceId: (virtualNetworkDeployBastion || subnet.name == 'AzureBastionSubnet')
              ? createBastionNsg.?outputs.resourceId
              : resourceId(
                  subscriptionId,
                  virtualNetworkResourceGroupName,
                  'Microsoft.Network/networkSecurityGroups',
                  '${createLzNsg[i].?outputs.name}'
                )
            routeTableResourceId: (!empty(subnet.?routeTableName) && !empty(routeTablesResourceGroupName))
              ? resourceId(
                  subscriptionId,
                  routeTablesResourceGroupName,
                  'Microsoft.Network/routeTables',
                  subnet.?routeTableName ?? ''
                )
              : null
            natGatewayResourceId: virtualNetworkDeployNatGateway && (subnet.?associateWithNatGateway ?? false)
              ? createNatGateway.?outputs.resourceId
              : null
            delegation: subnet.?delegation
            serviceEndpoints: subnet.?serviceEndpoints
          }
        : {}
    ]
```

## Description

This PR adds the **FinOps Hub** pattern module to Azure Verified Modules (AVM). FinOps Hub is a comprehensive cost management and optimization solution that ingests, normalizes, and analyzes cloud cost data from multiple providers.

## CI Status (Fork)
[![avm.ptn.finops-toolkit.finops-hub](https://github.com/FallenHoot/bicep-registry-modules/actions/workflows/avm.ptn.finops-toolkit.finops-hub.yml/badge.svg?branch=feature/finops-hub-avm-module)](https://github.com/FallenHoot/bicep-registry-modules/actions/workflows/avm.ptn.finops-toolkit.finops-hub.yml)

## Features

- **Multi-cloud support**: Ingest FOCUS-compliant cost data from Azure, AWS, GCP, and OCI
- **Flexible analytics backend**: Choose between Azure Data Explorer (ADX) or Microsoft Fabric
- **Pre-built analytics**: KQL functions for cost analysis, optimization recommendations, and reporting
- **Security options**: Optional managed virtual network for enhanced data protection
- **WAF-aligned**: Deployment options that follow Azure Well-Architected Framework best practices
- **EXPERIMENTAL dashboard**: ADX dashboard JSON with 19 pages covering cost analysis, commitments, optimization, and multi-cloud views

## Module Details

| Attribute | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Module Path | `avm/ptn/finops-toolkit/finops-hub` |
| Version | 1.0.0 |
| Type | Pattern (ptn) |
| Telemetry | `46d3xbcp.ptn.finopstoolkit-finopshub` |

## AVM Compliance

- ✅ Implements `lock` and `diagnosticSettings` standard interfaces
- ✅ Uses AVM common types from `avm/utl/types/avm-common-types:0.6.1`
- ✅ Follows AVM naming conventions and module structure
- ✅ Includes comprehensive e2e tests for all deployment scenarios (7 tests)
- ✅ Telemetry enabled via `enableTelemetry` parameter
- ✅ PSRule WAF alignment checks passing

## Test Scenarios

All 7 e2e test scenarios are **enabled and passing**:

| Test | Description | Status |
|------|-------------|--------|
| storage-minimal | Basic deployment with storage-only defaults | ✅ |
| adx-minimal | Minimal ADX deployment | ✅ |
| adx-waf-aligned | WAF-aligned ADX with managed identities, diagnostics | ✅ |
| adx-managed-network | ADX with managed virtual network | ✅ |
| fabric-minimal | Minimal Fabric deployment | ✅ |
| fabric-waf-aligned | WAF-aligned Fabric deployment | ✅ |
| managed-network | Managed virtual network configuration | ✅ |

## ADX Managed Identity Policy — Implementation Note

The ADX cluster requires a `managed_identity` policy for native ingestion via Azure Data Factory. We explored several approaches to automate this:

1. **Deployment Script with `scriptLevel: 'Cluster'`** — Works in CI but the database script resource has limitations with cluster-level KQL commands in some edge cases.
2. **Cluster Principal Assignment** — Grants broad admin roles; not granular enough for just ingestion policy.
3. **Direct REST API via deployment scripts** — Requires bearer token management and adds deployment complexity.

**Current approach**: The ADX managed identity policy is set via an **ADF pipeline activity** (`Set Ingestion Policy`) that runs as part of the `ingestion_ETL_dataExplorer` pipeline. This mirrors the [upstream FinOps Toolkit](https://github.com/microsoft/finops-toolkit) pattern where ADF manages ADX configuration as part of the data pipeline, rather than during ARM deployment.

We've engaged the ADX Product Group for guidance on a cleaner Bicep-native approach (e.g., a dedicated ARM resource type for MI policy). In the meantime, the ADF-based approach is reliable and production-tested.

review_comments.author: FallenHoot
review_comments.body:
This module is retained as a **legacy reference only** and is **not wired into the deployment graph**. Per ADR-013, ADX does not natively support executing cluster-level management commands (e.g., `.alter-merge cluster policy managed_identity`) through ARM-deployable resources — `Microsoft.Kusto/clusters/databases/scripts` is limited to database-scoped commands, and deployment scripts face a known ARM→ADX control-plane timing gap where principal assignments have not yet propagated. This limitation has been reported to the ADX Product Group.

The accepted workaround is to set the managed identity policy at runtime via an ADF `AzureDataExplorerCommand` pipeline activity (the 'Set Ingestion Policy' step in `dataFactoryResources.bicep`). We keep this file in case the ADX PG addresses the platform limitation in a future API version. Since it's unused, extracting the inline script to an external file isn't needed at this time.

## Description

The `kind` parameter value passed to the web app module is being replaced with a hardcoded `'app,linux'` value when any kind is specified. This breaks Windows App Service deployments because the staging slot gets created as Linux while the production site is Windows.

Found during deployment testing - the conditional on line 190 in `app-service.module.bicep`:

kind: !empty(kind) ? 'app,linux' : 'app'

kind: kind

review_comments.author: eriqua
review_comments.body:
My main concern with this is that this would potentially result in a huge PR, which I personally don't support.

I believe it would be wiser to cover smaller scopes, for the time being, but optimizing it. Let's consider the API version check as an example. Updating the api version is not always as easy as changing the version. It involves new features, additional parameters, potentially, although not too often, even breaking changes. Not to mention new child resources. Depending on this, we should mention what version update we expect, major (not now), minor or patch. This is where we should leverage AI support imho. It's very much a skill on its own.

Once we have a few of those well scoped skills, we can think about implementing a "super skill".

I'd probably deprioritize content already fully covered by static validation. For example I'd avoid checking if we have waf-aligned and defaults tests. If we didn't, the module wouldn't be there. Note: the max test is not mandatory, so it's not correct to include it. Plus, "Deploys with all (or most) parameters set" is not providing clear guidance. Instead, what about: for a max test I would like to verify if all possible parameters are included and out of all possible parameters have a clear understanding of which parameters cannot be used together, as they would otherwise result in a conflict. Just food for thoughts

prs.body:
## Description

Fixes #5561

Adds Confidential VM (CVM) support to the `avm/res/compute/virtual-machine` and `avm/res/compute/virtual-machine-scale-set` modules.

### Defect 1: uefiSettings is null when securityType == ConfidentialVM

The `uefiSettings` condition only matched `TrustedLaunch`. When `securityType` is `ConfidentialVM`, `uefiSettings` evaluated to null. Azure requires `secureBootEnabled: true` and `vTpmEnabled: true` for Confidential VMs.

**Fix:** Changed the condition to include both security types.

### Defect 2: OS disk managedDisk.securityProfile.securityEncryptionType is missing (VM module only)

There was no `securityProfile` object on the managed disk. Azure requires `osDisk.managedDisk.securityProfile.securityEncryptionType` to be set for Confidential VMs.

**Fix:** Added optional `securityProfile` (with `securityEncryptionType` and `diskEncryptionSetResourceId`) to the `osDiskType` and wired it into the VM resource.

> Note: The VMSS module uses `resourceInput<>` for osDisk, which inherits the schema from the ARM API and already includes securityProfile. No change needed there.

### Defect 3: Misleading parameter descriptions

The descriptions for `secureBootEnabled` and `vTpmEnabled` only mentioned TrustedLaunch.

**Fix:** Updated descriptions to mention both TrustedLaunch and ConfidentialVM.

### E2E Test

Added `windows.confidentialvm` E2E test validating:

- `securityType: 'ConfidentialVM'`
- `uefiSettings` (secureBootEnabled + vTpmEnabled)
- `osDisk.managedDisk.securityProfile.securityEncryptionType: 'VMGuestStateOnly'`
- VM size: `Standard_DC2as_v5` (DCasv5-series)

prs.author: oZakari
prs.body:
## Description

Fixes #6900
Fixes #7125

The `customSubscriptionPlacement` module loop in `avm/ptn/mgmt-groups/subscription-placement` had an inverted condition. Subscriptions were only placed when `disableSubscriptionPlacement` was set to `true` — the opposite of the intended behaviour.

This change negates the condition (and uses `?? false` to safely handle the omitted/null case) so that:

- `disableSubscriptionPlacement` omitted → placement runs
- `disableSubscriptionPlacement: false` → placement runs
- `disableSubscriptionPlacement: true` → placement skipped

### Additional fix: e2e resource-removal helper (#7125)

While validating the fix, the e2e cleanup phase failed with `Cannot delete non-empty management group [test-mgmt-group]`. Root cause: `Get-DeploymentTargetResourceListInner` in `utilities/pipelines/e2eValidation/resourceRemoval/helper/Get-DeploymentTargetResourceList.ps1` reused the parent caller's `$ManagementGroupId` when recursing into managementGroup-scoped child deployments, instead of extracting the MG ID from the child deployment's resource path. The defaults test runs at tenant scope and nests deployments into newly-created MGs, so the recursive lookup queried the API with an empty MG ID and silently dropped the nested deployments (`Not found deployment ... Ignoring, as nested deployment.`). As a result `Microsoft.Subscription/aliases` was never enumerated for removal and the MG could not be deleted. The fix mirrors the existing subscription-path branch and extracts the actual MG ID from the deployment's resource path. See #7125 for full details.

prs.body:
## Description

The NetApp account module did not expose the Active Directory `site` field, which blocked parity with existing portal-configured AD integrations during migration to Bicep. This change adds an explicit module input and maps it to the ARM `activeDirectories[].site` property.

- **Module behavior**
  - Added new optional nullable parameter: `activeDirectorySite`.
  - Wired `activeDirectorySite` into `Microsoft.NetApp/netAppAccounts.properties.activeDirectories[].site`.
  - Emits `site` only when both `domainName` and `activeDirectorySite` are non-empty (avoids sending empty string values).

- **Generated artifacts**
  - Updated `main.json` to include the new parameter and compiled mapping.
  - Updated `README.md` to document `activeDirectorySite`, keep parameter ordering consistent, and clarify the site description.
  - Updated `CHANGELOG.md` with a new entry (`0.12.5`) for this enhancement.

```bicep
@description('Optional. The Active Directory site (as configured in Active Directory Sites and Services) the service will limit Domain Controller discovery to.')
param activeDirectorySite string?

var activeDirectoryConnectionProperties = [
  {
    // ...
    site: !empty(domainName) && !empty(activeDirectorySite) ? activeDirectorySite : null
  }
]
```

- **Test infrastructure**
  - Replaced the CMK test's sleep-only Azure deploymentScript with OIDC-authenticated runner-side dependency preparation and the same 15-second propagation wait.
  - Retained the actual CMK account deployment and cleanup tracking for both phases; no production-module changes were needed for this test fix and no Azure security controls were relaxed.

prs.body:
This change adds additive, per-notification control for budget alerts so a single budget can mix `Actual` and `Forecasted` notifications with independent operators. Existing behavior is preserved by keeping the current `thresholds` + `thresholdType` path as fallback when `notifications` is not provided.

- **Module contract changes (all scopes: sub/mg/rg)**
  - Added exported `notificationType` user-defined type with `operator`, bounded `threshold`, and `thresholdType`.
  - Added optional `@maxLength(5) param notifications notificationType[]?`.
  - Marked `thresholds` and `thresholdType` descriptions as deprecated in favor of `notifications`.

- **Notification composition logic**
  - When `notifications` is non-empty, resource notifications are built from it.
  - Otherwise, notifications are derived from legacy `thresholds` + `operator` + `thresholdType` to keep compatibility.

- **Generated module artifacts**
  - Regenerated scoped `README.md` and `main.json` files for `sub-scope`, `mg-scope`, and `rg-scope` via `Set-AVMModule`.

- **Versioning and CHANGELOG**
  - Bumped the MINOR version in `version.json` from `0.1` to `0.2` for all three scopes (`sub-scope`, `mg-scope`, `rg-scope`).
  - Added a `## 0.2.0` section to each scope's `CHANGELOG.md` describing the new `notifications` parameter. This resolves the Module Compliance failure requiring the CHANGELOG to contain a section for the new module version.

```bicep
param notifications notificationType[]?

var notificationSettings = !empty(notifications ?? []) ? notifications! : notificationsFromThresholds

var notificationsArray = [
  for notification in notificationSettings: {
    '${notification.thresholdType}_${notification.operator}_${notification.threshold}_Percentage': {
      enabled: true
      operator: notification.operator
      threshold: notification.threshold
      thresholdType: notification.thresholdType
    }
  }
]
```

prs.author: segraef
prs.body:
Improves the agent guidance for contributing to AVM Bicep modules and makes it work across AI assistants, not just GitHub Copilot.

## Changes

- **`.github/copilot-instructions.md`**: Added an explicit, mandatory ordered checklist for fixing an issue in an existing module - branch + contribution-model detection (maintainer direct-push vs fork), edit `main.bicep` only, bump `version.json`/`CHANGELOG.md`, regenerate `main.json` + `README.md` via `Set-AVMModule`, update e2e tests, local Pester gate before push, and e2e workflow + status badge on the PR. Also bumped the validated model to `Claude Opus 4.8` or `Fable`.
- **`AGENTS.md`**: Mirrors `.github/copilot-instructions.md` with an AGENTS.md-style header so non-Copilot agents (Claude Code, Cursor, and others) that read `AGENTS.md` get the same rules. Kept in sync with the instructions file.

## Why

Instructions are guidance, not enforcement, and agents were missing key steps (running `Set-AVMModule`, getting local tests green, attaching the e2e badge). The checklist makes those steps unmissable. `AGENTS.md` exists because non-Copilot assistants do not read `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, so the operative rules are duplicated there rather than redirected.

## Description
This pull request expands the set of disabled TLS cipher suites in the API Management service modules to enhance security and align with best practices. It updates the default security configuration in both the Bicep and JSON templates, documentation, and related tests to explicitly disable several additional ECDHE and RSA cipher suites.
Fixes #6167 
The most important changes are:

**Security configuration updates:**

* Added the following cipher suites to the default set of disabled ciphers in `customProperties` and related configuration:
  * `TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_AES_128_CBC_SHA`
  * `TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_AES_128_CBC_SHA256`
  * `TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_AES_256_CBC_SHA`
  * `TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_AES_256_CBC_SHA384`
  * `TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_256_CBC_SHA384`
  * `TLS_RSA_WITH_AES_256_GCM_SHA384`

**Documentation updates:**

* Updated `README.md` to document the new disabled cipher suites in all relevant code and configuration examples, ensuring users are aware of the expanded set of disabled ciphers. 

**Template and test updates:**

* Synchronized the changes in the generated ARM template (`main.json`) and end-to-end test configuration to reflect the updated set of disabled ciphers.

prs.author: PadhiAjit-Microsoft
prs.body:
## Description
This pull request introduces several new Bicep modules for Azure AI and search resources, as well as improvements to workflow automation and job execution controls. The most significant changes are the addition of reusable, parameterized modules to streamline the deployment of AI Foundry projects, AI model deployments, AI Search, and generic Cognitive Services resources. Additionally, workflow automation is enhanced with a new container migration workflow and improved job execution conditions for pull request labeling.

**New AI and Search Bicep Modules:**

* Added `ai-foundry-project.bicep`, a wrapper module for deploying an Azure AI Services account and an AI Foundry project, with outputs for resource IDs, endpoints, and identities.
* Added `ai-foundry-model-deployment.bicep` for deploying a single AI model to an existing AI Services account, supporting model format, version, RAI policy, and SKU configuration.
* Added `ai-foundry-connection.bicep` to create a parameterized connection on an AI Foundry project, supporting various categories (e.g., CognitiveSearch, AzureBlob) and authentication types.
* Added `ai-search.bicep`, which implements a two-step deployment pattern for Azure AI Search: a fast initial resource creation, followed by an AVM module update for full configuration and managed identity.
* Added `ai-services.bicep`, a generic AVM wrapper for deploying Cognitive Services accounts of various kinds (e.g., ContentSafety, Speech, OpenAI), with support for private networking and role assignments.

**Workflow Automation and Controls:**

* Introduced `.github/workflows/avm.ptn.sa.container-migration.yml`, a new workflow for AVM container migration with input parameters for validation and deployment control, and a two-job structure for initialization and execution.
* Updated `platform.set-avm-github-pr-labels.yml` to skip the label-setting job on forks, preventing failures due to missing GitHub App secrets and aligning with existing fork-handling patterns.

## Summary

Upgrade the AVM FinOps hub pattern from the legacy FinOps Toolkit 0.3 implementation to the current Toolkit v14 package. This enables the wrapper to deploy Azure Data Explorer or Fabric analytics, including the Hub and Ingestion databases required by current FinOps dashboards.

## Changes

- replace the embedded Toolkit 0.3 hub implementation with Toolkit v14
- add Azure Data Explorer and Fabric analytics configuration and outputs
- retain `exportScopes` as a deprecated compatibility alias for `scopesToMonitor`
- add Data Explorer and WAF-aligned end-to-end scenarios
- update the workflow, changelog, generated README, and compiled ARM template
- advance the module version line from 0.1 to 0.2

## Migration notes

- removes legacy `configContainer`, `exportContainer`, `ingestionContainer`, and `convertToParquet` parameters
- managed exports use the Toolkit v14 default and require the hub identity to receive Role Based Access Control Administrator on the hub storage account
- adds `clusterId`, `clusterUri`, `ingestionDbName`, and `hubDbName` outputs
- defaults Data Explorer capacity to one node for Dev/Test SKUs and two nodes for Standard SKUs

prs.author: myaschmitz
prs.body:
## Description

The "Pre-flight check" block mandated two things: emit a JSON block self-reporting agent-mode and model, and warn the user if the model is not `Claude Opus 4.6` while pointing them at a `/AVM-Boostrap` prompt. This PR keeps the first and drops the second.

Two defects with the warning:

- **`/AVM-Boostrap` does not exist.** `.github/prompts/` contains three files, none of them a bootstrap prompt, and `git grep -i boostrap` returns exactly one hit — the sentence telling users to run it. It is also misspelled (missing the second `t`), which suggests it was never exercised.
- **The `Claude Opus 4.6` pin rots by design.** It was added in #6751 when Opus 4.6 was current and has never been updated, so every model released since then trips the warning. Nothing consumes this file programmatically (`git grep -ril copilot-instructions` outside the file itself returns nothing) — it is prose injected into model context, so the warning cannot actually change anyone's configuration. Its only effect is to tell contributors on current models that they are misconfigured and point them at a prompt that does not exist.

Bumping the pin to a newer model was considered and rejected: it resets the same clock.

**Kept:** the mandatory `agent-mode` / `model` JSON self-report, plus one sentence noting it is there so the configuration is visible when a transcript is shared for triage.

**Removed:** the version comparison, the "untested configuration" warning, and the `/AVM-Boostrap` instruction.

## Pipeline Reference

Not applicable — docs-only change to `.github/copilot-instructions.md`. No module, template, or workflow is touched.

- [x] My corresponding pipelines / checks run clean and green without any errors or warnings

This pull request introduces significant enhancements and some breaking changes to the `customer-chatbot` solution, primarily focused on expanding deployment capabilities, updating default AI models, and improving resource output structure. The most important changes are summarized below.

**Major enhancements and resource updates:**

* Added support for deploying an Azure Container Registry (ACR) resource, including managed identity-based ACR Pull role assignments. ([avm/ptn/sa/customer-chatbot/CHANGELOG.mdR5-R19](diffhunk://#diff-4f5edded6ca0da2e35e3b9f5bfec5aad23e469d0120590be1178d1316d8949e9R5-R19), Fb18ce3fL573R573)
* Split web apps into separate chat (frontend/backend) and scenario (frontend/backend) services, and updated outputs to reflect these new resources. ([avm/ptn/sa/customer-chatbot/CHANGELOG.mdR5-R19](diffhunk://#diff-4f5edded6ca0da2e35e3b9f5bfec5aad23e469d0120590be1178d1316d8949e9R5-R19), Fb18ce3fL586R586)
* Added Cosmos DB and Cognitive Services role assignments for the scenario backend.

**AI model and deployment configuration updates:**

* Updated the default GPT model to `gpt-5.4-mini` (version `2026-03-17`) and set the default image tag to `"latest"`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-4f5edded6ca0da2e35e3b9f5bfec5aad23e469d0120590be1178d1316d8949e9R5-R19) Fb18ce3fL333R333, Fb18ce3fL481R481, [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-e64e2cd2c50fd9ba54d452cac19ce6f52b78635374e2df3fb9c2f3e5e38abd2cL34-R34)
* Changed AI Services `publicNetworkAccess` to always enabled, with private endpoint configuration handled separately.

**Documentation and workflow improvements:**

* Updated the README to document new resources, parameters, and outputs, including ACR and the new web app services. Removed deprecated parameters and outputs (e.g., `containerRegistryHost`, `webAppUrl`). (Fb18ce3fL8R8, Fb18ce3fL57R57, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-a7ac5497ac5e48e334fbfb0af2154dd633cc4a6a00a42180ea76f7e7196d91bcL323) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a7ac5497ac5e48e334fbfb0af2154dd633cc4a6a00a42180ea76f7e7196d91bcL383-L390) Fb18ce3fL559R559, Fb18ce3fL573R573, Fb18ce3fL586R586)
* Added a new GitHub Actions workflow for container migration (`.github/workflows/avm.ptn.sa.container-migration.yml`).
* Improved workflow security by restricting PR label setting to the upstream repository only.

**Breaking changes:**

* The structure of web app resources and some output variables has changed. Review the changelog and updated outputs for migration guidance. ([avm/ptn/sa/customer-chatbot/CHANGELOG.mdR5-R19](diffhunk://#diff-4f5edded6ca0da2e35e3b9f5bfec5aad23e469d0120590be1178d1316d8949e9R5-R19), Fb18ce3fL586R586)

These updates enhance modularity, security, and future compatibility for the `customer-chatbot` deployment.

prs.author: PadhiAjit-Microsoft
prs.body:
## Description
This pull request introduces several new Bicep modules and updates to support AVM v2 modularization for the "chat-with-your-data" solution. The changes provide generic, reusable modules for deploying and managing Azure AI resources, including AI Foundry projects, model deployments, connections, AI Search, and Cognitive Services accounts. These modules are designed for flexibility, improved maintainability, and alignment with Azure Well-Architected Framework (WAF) best practices.

**Key module additions and updates:**

**AI Foundry and Cognitive Services Modularization**
- Added `ai-foundry-project.bicep` to provision both AI Services accounts and AI Foundry projects with AVM best practices, supporting custom naming, identity, networking, and outputs for endpoints and identities.
- Added `ai-services.bicep` as a generic wrapper for deploying various Cognitive Services resources, supporting multiple kinds, private networking, role assignments, and telemetry.

**Model Deployment and Connection Modules**
- Introduced `ai-foundry-model-deployment.bicep` for deploying AI models to existing AI Services accounts, supporting flexible model formats, SKUs, and Responsible AI (RAI) policy.
- Added `ai-foundry-connection.bicep` for creating parameterized, reusable connections to AI Foundry projects, supporting multiple connection categories and authentication types.

**AI Search Modularization**
- Added `ai-search.bicep` module implementing a two-step deployment pattern for Azure AI Search, enabling fast resource creation followed by AVM-based configuration and managed identity enablement.

**Documentation**
- Updated the changelog to reflect the AVM v2 modularization and upgradation, with no breaking changes.

Sourced from axios's releases.

v1.18.0 — June 13, 2026

This release hardens redirect and URL handling, improves the validateStatus configuration semantics, and includes updates to documentation, dependencies, and release metadata.

🔒 Security Fixes

  • Redirect Header Safety: Added Node HTTP adapter support for stripping caller-specified sensitive headers on cross-origin redirects, helping prevent custom auth headers such as API keys from leaking to another origin. (#10892)

  • URL And Request Hardening: Rejects malformed http: and https: URLs that omit // with ERR_INVALID_URL, while tightening prototype-pollution-safe config reads, stream size limits, FormData depth handling, data URL sizing, and local NO_PROXY matching. (#11000)

🐛 Bug Fixes

  • Status Validation: Added transitional.validateStatusUndefinedResolves so applications can opt in to treating validateStatus: undefined like the option was omitted, while validateStatus: null remains the explicit way to accept every status. (#10899)

🔧 Maintenance & Chores

  • Documentation: Published the v1.17.0 release notes, fixed a changelog typo, clarified the package update PR policy, and marked the proxy request config as Node.js-only in the advanced docs. (#10984, #10988, #10992, #10995)

  • Dependencies: Bumped @babel/core, @babel/preset-env, @commitlint/cli, @commitlint/config-conventional, @rollup/plugin-babel, @rollup/plugin-commonjs, @vitest/browser, @vitest/browser-playwright, eslint, lint-staged, rollup, vitest, and actions/checkout. (#10989, #10996, #10997)

v1.17.0 — June 1, 2026

This release adds Node HTTP zstd decompression, hardens config and release workflows, and fixes authentication, header, proxy, and type-handling regressions.

🔒 Security Fixes

  • Config Hardening: Guarded socketPath, params, and paramsSerializer reads with own-property checks to prevent inherited prototype values from affecting request behavior, including SSRF-sensitive paths. (#10901, #10922)
  • Release Publishing: Switched the publish workflow to npm staged publishing for safer, auditable package releases with provenance. (#10926)

🚀 New Features

  • HTTP Compression: Added Node HTTP adapter support for zstd response decompression, with transitional.advertiseZstdAcceptEncoding controlling whether zstd is advertised in Accept-Encoding. (#6792, #10920)

🐛 Bug Fixes

  • Authentication Handling: Restored Basic auth on same-origin Node redirects while continuing to strip credentials cross-origin, and aligned the fetch adapter with HTTP adapter behavior for URL-embedded Basic auth. (#10929, #10896)
  • Proxy TLS: Preserved user httpsAgent TLS options when tunneling HTTPS requests through HTTP CONNECT proxies. (#10957)
  • React Native FormData: Cleared default Content-Type for React Native FormData so multipart boundaries can be generated correctly. (#10898)

prs.body:
## Description

The `deployments` parameter defaulted each item's name to `'${name}-deployments'`, so any account with more than one model deployment generated duplicate `Microsoft.CognitiveServices/accounts/deployments` resource names and failed validation:

```
InvalidTemplate: The resource 'Microsoft.CognitiveServices/accounts/aoai-devdtzp/deployments/aoai-devdtzp-deployments'
at line '1' and column '34876' is defined multiple times in a template.
```

As suggested in the issue discussion, the default only ever made sense for exactly one deployment, so `name` becomes required rather than silently collision-prone.

- **`main.bicep`**: `deploymentType.name` changed from `string?` to `string` (`Required`); the loop now passes `deploymentConfiguration.name` instead of falling back to `'${name}-deployments'`.
- **Tests**: added a second model deployment to the `ai-model-deployment` e2e test to exercise the multi-deployment path. All other e2e tests already set an explicit name, so no other test changes were needed.
- **Versioning**: `version.json` bumped to `0.20`, with a CHANGELOG entry recording the breaking change.
- **Generated files**: `main.json` and the READMEs regenerated via `Set-AVMModule`.

Consumers relying on the implicit name must now specify it:

```bicep
deployments: [
  {
    name: 'gpt-35-turbo'          // now required
    model: { name: 'gpt-35-turbo', format: 'OpenAI', version: '0125' }
    sku: { name: 'Standard', capacity: 8 }
  }
  {
    name: 'dall-e-3'
    model: { name: 'dall-e-3', format: 'OpenAI', version: '3.0' }
    sku: { name: 'Standard', capacity: 1 }
  }
]
```

## Description

- Updated the `Microsoft.Databricks/workspaces` API version from `2024-05-01` to `2026-01-01`.
- Added the optional parameter `computeMode`, which the newer API version declares as required. It is written through a conditional spread, so it is only sent when supplied and existing deployments are unaffected.

### Why

On `2024-05-01` the resource provider refuses to change the subnets of an existing VNet-injected workspace. Repointing `customPublicSubnetName` / `customPrivateSubnetName` fails the deployment with:

```
PublicSubnetNamePropertyChangeNotAllowed
Updating required Public Subnet Name from <old> to <new> is allowed in
api-version 2025-02-01-preview or beyond
```

The provider names the remedy itself. Of the versions at or beyond that point, `2026-01-01` is the first stable one and the rest are previews, so that is the version this module moves to.

Without it, a workspace deployed by this module cannot be moved onto different subnets through the module at all.

### Compatibility

The schema difference between the two versions is additive. The `parameters` object has an identical key set, and `computeMode` is the only addition at the top level of `properties`.

Because `2026-01-01` declares `computeMode` required, leaving it unset raises `BCP035`. It is therefore exposed as `string?` and written as `...(computeMode != null ? { computeMode: computeMode! } : {})`, matching the conditional-spread style the module already uses for `customVirtualNetworkResourceId`. With that shape the module builds free of BCP diagnostics, and callers that do not set it produce the same request body as before.

prs.author: chirag1603
prs.body:
## Description

Fixes #7394

On `avm/res/azure-stack-hci/cluster`, when `Validate` and `Deploy` are run as **two separate module invocations** (the recommended Azure Local pattern — validate as a gate, then deploy), the portal cluster **Deployments** blade shows **"Validate input = Unknown"** even though **Deploy** is green and the cluster is healthy.

### Root cause

The inline cluster deployment script (`src/deploy.sh`) deleted the singleton `deploymentSettings/default` resource whenever a Deploy run found it left in **Validate** mode:

```
if [ "$DEPLOYMENT_MODE" = "Validate" ]; then
    echo "Removing stale Validate-mode resource..."
    az resource delete --ids ".../deploymentSettings/default"
```

Deleting and recreating the resource in Deploy-only mode discards the RP-reported `reportedProperties.validationStatus` written during Validate, so the portal "Validate input" tile has nothing to read → **Unknown**.

### Why the delete is avoidable (grounded)

The `Validate` → `Deploy` transition updates the **same** resource in place — no delete is required:

- **Azure Quickstart** [`create-cluster`](https://github.com/Azure/azure-quickstart-templates/tree/master/quickstarts/microsoft.azurestackhci/create-cluster) exposes a single `deploymentMode` parameter (`Validate` | `Deploy`, default `Validate`, *"First must pass Validate prior running Deploy"*) and **redeploys the same resource** with the mode changed — no delete step.
- **[ARM deployment modes (Microsoft Learn)](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-resource-manager/templates/deployment-modes):** the default Incremental mode **updates resources in place and deletes nothing** unless type/location changes or Complete mode is used.
- **This module's own nested loop** (`modules/deployment-setting.bicep`) already transitions `Validate` → `Deploy` on the same `default` singleton via two sequential deployments (`@batchSize(1)`, Validate first) with **no delete** — proving the in-place transition works.

### The change

In `src/deploy.sh`, a **succeeded** Validate resource is no longer deleted — the script redeploys `Deploy` over it in place, preserving `validationStatus`. A **non-succeeded/stale** Validate resource is still removed (clean-retry safeguard). `main.json` was regenerated via `Set-AVMModule`.

This is **cosmetic and preventive**: it does not repair already-deployed clusters (a `Deploy + Succeeded` singleton hits the script's idempotency skip), but it keeps both portal tiles green for future deployments.

### Testing

- `Set-AVMModule` regenerated `main.json` (script is inlined via `loadTextContent`); interface/README unchanged.
- `bicep lint main.bicep` — clean (exit 0); `bash -n src/deploy.sh` — clean.
- Static-validation Pester suite (`module.tests.ps1`) scoped to the module: **91 passed, 9 skipped (N/A features)**. The single failure is the pre-existing, repo-wide *"issue template alphabetical position"* check (lists only unrelated `avm/ptn/*` modules; not touched by this PR).
- No live end-to-end run: the target behavior is grounded in the sources above; an already-deployed cluster cannot exercise the changed path due to the idempotency skip.

comments_list.body:
### Validation evidence (exercised against a live Azure Local deployment)

The rewritten `src/deploy.sh` was run end-to-end against a real Azure Local (Azure Stack HCI) cluster resource to confirm the fix behaves as intended.

**1. Two-phase split is real.**
With `deploymentOperations` including `Validate`, the script issued the validation as its **own** `az deployment group create` (a dedicated `hci-deployment-validate-<epoch>` deployment), separate from the Deploy operation — matching the ARM quickstart's "Validate first, then Deploy" flow instead of fusing both into a single deployment.

**2. `validationStatus` is retained on the resource (the actual fix).**
After the Validate phase, querying the cluster's `deploymentSettings/default` returned a **non-empty** `reportedProperties.validationStatus`:

```
deploymentMode:  Validate
validationEmpty: false      # validationStatus is populated, not wiped
```

A populated `validationStatus` is exactly what keeps the portal **"Validate input"** tile from falling back to **Unknown**. Under the previous script, a Validate-mode resource was unconditionally deleted before Deploy, which erased this record and produced the Unknown tile.

**3. No delete of a succeeded Validate.**
The Deploy phase now deploys **in place** over the existing `default` resource; only a stale / non-succeeded Validate is removed. This preserves the validation record across the Validate → Deploy transition.

**Coverage.** All three `deploymentOperations` combinations — `['Validate']`, `['Deploy']`, and `['Validate','Deploy']` — follow the same in-place, no-wipe path, so both portal tiles stay populated. The module's public interface is unchanged (backward compatible), and existing idempotency semantics (`Deploy` + `Succeeded` ⇒ skip; `Deploy` + not-succeeded ⇒ fail) are preserved.

## Description

- Added the optional parameter `customerManagedKeyDbfsRoot` (`customerManagedKeyType`), which encrypts the workspace's DBFS root storage account with a customer-managed key through `properties.parameters.encryption`. Key Vault and Managed HSM keys are both supported, following the same pattern as `customerManagedKey` and `customerManagedKeyManagedDisk`.
- Added the output `storageAccountIdentityPrincipalId`, the identity of the DBFS root storage account that needs access to that key. It is available once `prepareEncryption` is enabled, matching how `managedDiskIdentityPrincipalId` is exposed for the managed disk key.
- Added the e2e test `cmk-dbfs`.

### Why

The module supports customer-managed keys for managed services and managed disks, but not for the third feature Azure Databricks offers, the DBFS root. A workspace that must use customer-managed keys for all data at rest, as PCI DSS and similar regimes expect, cannot be expressed through the module today.

The storage account identity is created by the provider when `prepareEncryption` is set, and it must hold `Key Vault Crypto Service Encryption User` on the key before the key is applied. The module had that identity commented out as read only and did not output it, so a caller had no way to grant it without reading the resource back separately.

### How it is used

The key cannot be applied in the same deployment that first creates the identity, because the grant has to exist in between. The new test shows the sequence:

1. Deploy the workspace with `prepareEncryption: true`.
2. Grant `storageAccountIdentityPrincipalId` `Key Vault Crypto Service Encryption User` on the key.
3. Deploy the workspace again with `customerManagedKeyDbfsRoot` (then an idempotency run).

Without `keyVersion` the storage account follows the latest key version. Verified outside this repository on a VNet-injected premium workspace: all three customer-managed key features enabled together, a redeploy that omits `parameters.encryption` leaves the DBFS root key in place (no write reaches the storage account), and jobs run normally afterwards.

### Compatibility

Additive. The parameter is optional and the encryption block is written through a conditional spread, so callers that do not set it produce the same request body as before. `parameters.encryption` exists at the module's current API version `2024-05-01`; the module builds free of BCP diagnostics.

### Relation to #7381

Independent of #7381 (API version `2026-01-01` and `computeMode`), and based on `main`. Both bump `version.json` to `0.13` and touch `CHANGELOG.md`, `README.md` and `main.json`, so whichever merges second needs a rebase and the next minor version. Happy to rebase this one onto #7381 instead if the reviewer prefers a single release.

## Description

# Static Site Private DNS Deployment Issue

## Initial Issue

The deployment failed with the following errors:

`Warning BCP318:
The value of type "module | null" may be null at the start of the deployment.`
`Error InvalidTemplate:
The template resource '...-staticSite-PrivateEndpoint-0' reference to
'...-staticSite-PrivateDnsZone' requires an API version.`

The affected code in modules/Microsoft.Web/static-site/main.bicep was:
`privateDnsZoneGroup: privateEndpoint.?privateDnsZoneGroup ?? {
  privateDnsZoneGroupConfigs: [
    {
      privateDnsZoneResourceId: staticSite_privateDnsZone.outputs.resourceId
    }
  ]
}`

### Root Cause
The staticSite_privateDnsZone module is deployed conditionally:
`createPrivateDnsZone == 'Enabled'`

When createPrivateDnsZone is set to Disabled, the module is not deployed. However, the fallback expression in the ?? operator still contains a reference to the module:
`staticSite_privateDnsZone.outputs.resourceId`

The Bicep ?? operator is compiled to the ARM coalesce() function. ARM can evaluate the fallback expression even when an existing privateDnsZoneGroup has already been supplied.

As a result, ARM attempts to resolve a reference to a module that was not deployed. Since the reference does not contain a resolvable API version, the deployment fails with the InvalidTemplate error.

The same reference also causes warning BCP318, because the conditional module can be null.

### Solution
The module reference must be placed inside a conditional expression:
`privateDnsZoneGroup: privateEndpoint.?privateDnsZoneGroup ?? (createPrivateDnsZone == 'Enabled'
  ? {
      privateDnsZoneGroupConfigs: [
        {
          privateDnsZoneResourceId: staticSite_privateDnsZone!.outputs.resourceId
        }
      ]
    }
  : null)`

The expression now behaves as follows:

If privateEndpoint.privateDnsZoneGroup is provided, that configuration is used.
If no DNS zone group is provided and createPrivateDnsZone is Enabled, the resource ID of the newly created DNS zone is used.
If no DNS zone group is provided and createPrivateDnsZone is Disabled, the value is set to null.

## Description

Fixes the failed publishing of `avm/res/azure-stack-hci/virtual-machine-instance` `0.2.0` after #7429.

The module pipeline on `main` ([run 36736704112](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/actions/runs/36736704112)) failed the static test *"Set-ModuleReadMe script should not apply any updates"*, so `0.2.0` was not published. ## Description

Fix a cross-resource-group naming collision risk in the shared diagnostic test dependency helper. Storage account names now combine up to 11 base-name characters with a 13-character `uniqueString(resourceGroup().id, fullBase)` suffix (maximum 24 characters). Event Hubs namespace names combine up to 36 base-name characters, a hyphen, and the same form of suffix (maximum 50 characters).

The suffix is a deterministic, pseudorandom-looking hash, not cryptographic randomness or a guarantee against collisions. Names remain stable for the same resource group and inputs across initial deployments, repeat deployments, and retries. Including the full base name in the hash differentiates inputs that share a truncated prefix. Parameter descriptions explain this behavior.

Only the shared test helper and its regression tests change. Resource-group-scoped names, resources, role conditions, output IDs, and API versions are unchanged. No public AVM module, README, version, or generated module JSON changes.

prs.author: jaredfholgate
prs.body:
## Description

Use one generic validation-settings interface in all three reusable module workflows. Remove the tenant selector based on repository identity or module canaries: the consumer no longer reads `AVM_TEST_TENANT`, `TEST_BAMI_MODULE_PATHS`, or `TEST_BAMI_*` execution settings. Existing repository checks that protect release/tag creation are unchanged.

Execution identifiers may be configured as GitHub **Variables or Secrets**, with Variables taking precedence. The coordinated Tools publisher will use the canonical, nonsecret `VALIDATE_*` **Variables**. Actual credential JSON, passwords, and private keys are not moved to Variables; `AZURE_CREDENTIALS` remains Secrets-only.

### Identifier resolution and compatibility

| Setting | Resolution order |
| --- | --- |
| Client | `vars.VALIDATE_CLIENT_ID`, then `secrets.VALIDATE_CLIENT_ID` |
| Tenant | `vars.VALIDATE_TENANT_ID`, then `secrets.VALIDATE_TENANT_ID` |
| Subscription pool | `vars.VALIDATE_SUBSCRIPTION_IDS`, `vars.TEST_SUBSCRIPTION_IDS`, `secrets.VALIDATE_SUBSCRIPTION_IDS`, `secrets.TEST_SUBSCRIPTION_IDS` |
| Optional singleton | `vars.VALIDATE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID`, then `secrets.VALIDATE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID`; used only when no pool is configured |
| Management group | `vars.VALIDATE_MANAGEMENT_GROUP_ID`, `vars.ARM_MGMTGROUP_ID`, `secrets.VALIDATE_MANAGEMENT_GROUP_ID`, `secrets.ARM_MGMTGROUP_ID` |
| Persistent subscription | The publisher's canonical name is `VALIDATE_PERSISTENT_SUBSCRIPTION_ID`. These actions do not introduce a new input, required field, or token for this previously unused setting. |

Canonical names win within each namespace; Variables win across the existing aliases before Secrets. The values are mapped into the existing action inputs and runtime environment names. A supplied malformed pool is rejected, and a nonempty whitespace pool fails at the action boundary instead of silently selecting a singleton. The generic subscription helper API is unchanged.

### Authentication and contributor capabilities

Default OIDC authentication requires only its existing client and tenant identifiers, plus the selected subscription. It does not gain an unrelated management-group or five-setting requirement.

The existing service-principal exception path and both exception login steps remain available. When that path is used, credentials must be a JSON object with nonempty string `clientId`, `clientSecret`, and `tenantId` fields. Errors do not dump the credential payload. If `VALIDATE_TENANT_ID` is explicitly resolved, the credential tenant must match it case-insensitively. A **different same-tenant exception principal remains supported**; client equality is not imposed. Extra credential properties and selected-subscription replacement are preserved. Credential-only exception configurations remain supported when no separate tenant/client is configured. Exception paths and their descendants do not fall back to OIDC when credentials are missing, malformed, or inconsistent.

PSRule resolves a pool or singleton when configured and retains its optional static/no-auth behavior when neither is supplied. No new credential requirement is added to static analysis.

**Key Vault support is preserved.** The optional `KeyVaultName` API, existing `CI_KEY_VAULT_NAME` configuration and deprecation warning, vault lookup, GitHub CI_ secret-over-variable-over-vault precedence, type conversion, redaction, subscription fallback API, composite `managementGroupId` inputs, and selected-subscription reuse remain intact. Earlier out-of-scope removals were reversed and are not part of the final change.

### LIVE CUTOVER HOLD

Source publication does not authorize or perform runtime configuration changes. The coordinating parent must stage and verify the five canonical `VALIDATE_*` Variables, inspect collisions and effective inputs, and coordinate migration before resuming consumer execution. These names can be staged without overwriting the old `TEST_SUBSCRIPTION_IDS` or `ARM_MGMTGROUP_ID` settings used by unchanged maintenance workflows. Historical `TEST_BAMI_*` settings stay intact until their consumers migrate; this change does not delete them.

If canonical settings are missing, configured compatibility aliases or Secrets can become effective. The generic consumer **does not independently know which tenant is BAMI**. An `AZURE_CREDENTIALS` value used for an exception must target the explicitly declared tenant; credential-only configurations cannot be independently checked against an absent declared tenant. Operators must also review the intended `CI_KEY_VAULT_NAME` and its access in the chosen tenant. No existing secret is queried, deleted, or repaired by this source change.

## Final source scope

Against original baseline `82bab0404566557b9fb5efdc9780bb5ce438030b`, exactly six files change:

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `.github/workflows/avm.template.module.yml` | Generic Variables-first identifier bindings; no tenant selector. |
| `.github/workflows/avm.template.module.preview.yml` | The same generic bindings. |
| `.github/workflows/avm.template.module.publish.yml` | The same generic bindings. |
| `.github/actions/templates/avm-validateModuleDeployment/action.yml` | Method-required authentication checks, explicit tenant consistency, and supplied-pool whitespace rejection. |
| `.github/actions/templates/avm-validateModulePSRule/action.yml` | Optional generic pool/singleton resolution without a provider-specific branch. |
| `utilities/tests/pipelines/TestSubscriptionWorkflow.Tests.ps1` | Synthetic source/alias precedence, preserved capability, safe authentication-failure, and optional-static cases. |

Standalone PSRule/history workflows, generic helpers, other capability/regression tests, all module fixtures/APIs/versions, and the removed five-setting helper remain unchanged from the restored baseline. Nine specifically preserved files are byte/blob-identical to that baseline. No input API, normal trigger, fork/trust boundary, protected environment, permission, fixture matrix, `e2eIgnore`, release/tag guard, concurrency rule, retry policy, cancellation rule, or resource/history-cleanup behavior is removed.

## Pipeline Reference

| Offline verification | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Seven covering Pester suites | **588 passed; 0 failed; 0 skipped** |
| Workflow lint | All three reusable workflows pass actionlint |
| YAML/PowerShell parsing | 5 YAML files, 1 PowerShell file, 20 embedded scripts |
| Focused formatting/analyzer/whitespace | Pass; synthetic Key Vault test values have an explicit fixture-only analyzer suppression |
| Guard/interface proof | 562 unchanged workflow/action properties checked against baseline |
| Scope/capability proof | Exactly six files; nine preserved files remain byte/blob-identical |

Suites: `TestSubscriptionWorkflow`, `Get-TestSubscriptionList`, `CIParameterWorkflow`, `Get-CIParameterMap`, `RegionalValidationWorkflow`, `DeploymentCleanupWorkflow`, and `ModuleWorkflow`.

The tests cover Variables-only, Secrets-only, both sources, cross-alias precedence, optional singleton fallback, retired-selector independence, malformed preferred values, Key Vault warning/lookup/precedence, separate same-tenant exception principals, credential-only exceptions, mismatched tenants, safe credential errors, optional static PSRule, and existing retry/cleanup/fork/release behavior. Azure/network boundaries are mocked. No Azure authentication, cloud queries, deployments, manual workflow runs, live configuration changes, or blanket module test sweep were performed. Source CI is not evidence that all modules passed live end-to-end tests.

Exact tested head: `d4749cee573741524fc478b10ff199cdc9ee3149`.

Exact tested tree: `28a60606fb08e8fad88f7248c13028c1ba0269d1`.

## Type of Change

## Checklist

- [x] Reused the same open review and branch with a normal follow-up commit; no amend, rebase, or force push.
- [x] Preserved the externally selected ready-for-review state and existing labels; no auto-merge enabled.
- [x] Verified the exact source scope and offline tests on the committed tree.
- [ ] `Set-AVMModule` / module CHANGELOG updates — not applicable; no Bicep modules changed.
- [ ] Live namespace cutover or module deployments — on hold, not performed.

The coordinating parent retains responsibility for review, merge, and every live configuration decision. This source publication performs none of those actions.

## Description

Updates `avm/res/hybrid-container-service/provisioned-cluster-instance` so that the unpublished `0.3.0` can create clusters on Azure Local and passes the static tests again: it updates the referenced `connected-cluster` module, the Key Vault and telemetry API versions, and keeps `provisionedClusterInstances` on the stable `2024-01-01`.

| Resource type or reference | Published `0.2.1` | `main` (unpublished `0.3.0`) | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Microsoft.HybridContainerService/provisionedClusterInstances` | `2024-01-01` | `2026-04-01-preview` | `2024-01-01` |
| `avm/res/kubernetes/connected-cluster` (module and its 4 imported types) | `0.1.1` | `0.1.1` | `0.3.0` (deploys `connectedClusters` at `2026-05-01`) |
| `Microsoft.Kubernetes/connectedClusters` (`existing` reference) | `2024-07-15-preview` | `2024-07-15-preview` | `2026-05-01` |
| `Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults`, `vaults/secrets` | `2023-07-01` | `2023-07-01` | `2026-02-01` |
| `Microsoft.Resources/deployments` (AVM telemetry) | `2024-03-01` | `2024-03-01` | `2025-04-01` |

### Why `provisionedClusterInstances` stays on `2024-01-01`

#6995 moved `main` to `2026-04-01-preview` and added `hciSecurityProfile` (FIPS images, custom CA trust certificates), `gpuCountPerNode` and `authorizedIPRanges`. That version was never published, because the module's pipeline has stopped at static validation since then. Creating a cluster with it fails on Azure Local:

- Azure Resource Manager accepts `2023-11-15-preview`, `2024-01-01` and `2026-04-01-preview` for this resource type.
- A create is only forwarded if the AKS Arc extension behind the Azure Local custom location supports the API version. On the Azure Local release used for validation it supports `2023-11-15-preview` to `2025-09-01-preview`, so a create at `2026-04-01-preview` fails at preflight with `MissingAzureKubernetesMapping` ("The custom location ... does not support resource type 'Microsoft.HybridContainerService/provisionedClusterInstances' with api-version '2026-04-01-preview'"). Reads at `2026-04-01-preview` work.
- The [AKS release notes for Azure Local](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/aks-hybrid-edge/local/aks-whats-new-local) list no AKS changes since release 2602.

`2024-01-01` is therefore the newest version that both accept, and the one the published `0.2.1` uses. It has no `securityProfile` and no `gpuCountPerNode`; the [API change log](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/templates/microsoft.hybridcontainerservice/change-log/provisionedclusterinstances) lists both as added in `2026-04-01-preview`. This PR therefore removes the `hciSecurityProfile` parameter, its exported `hciSecurityProfileType`, and `gpuCountPerNode` from `agentPoolProfileType`. None of them was ever published, so no released version breaks. `authorizedIPRanges` exists in `2024-01-01` and stays. The removed settings can come back once Azure Local supports an API version that has them.

### Schema impact

A diff of the PUT body schemas of [`2026-04-01-preview`](https://github.com/Azure/azure-rest-api-specs/blob/b51b4e628385a62aa5199ee9bf06bb6b61a681eb/specification/hybridaks/resource-manager/Microsoft.HybridContainerService/HybridContainerService/preview/2026-04-01-preview/openapi.json) and [`2024-01-01`](https://github.com/Azure/azure-rest-api-specs/blob/b51b4e628385a62aa5199ee9bf06bb6b61a681eb/specification/hybridaks/resource-manager/Microsoft.HybridContainerService/HybridContainerService/stable/2024-01-01/provisionedClusterInstances.json) shows:

- `2024-01-01` lacks `securityProfile` (and its sub-properties), `agentPoolProfiles[].gpuCountPerNode` and the read-only `status.featuresStatus`.
- `networkProfile.networkPolicy` doesn't accept `cilium` in `2024-01-01`; the module's default is `calico`, as in `0.2.1`.
- All 26 other property paths the module sets exist in `2024-01-01`.

The referenced `connected-cluster` module moves from `0.1.1` to `0.3.0`: the 4 imported types (`aadProfileType`, `arcAgentProfileType`, `oidcIssuerProfileType`, `securityProfileType`) have the same structure in both versions, and every parameter this module passes still exists. Its `0.2.0` and `0.3.0` list no breaking changes.

The Key Vault references are in `secrets.bicep` and in `nested/read.bicep` and `nested/write.bicep`, which the module's SSH-key deployment script deploys to read and store the generated key pair. #7374 updates Key Vault references in other modules to at least `2026` because of a pending API deprecation; this module wasn't included there.

### Static tests that fail on `main`

- `CHANGELOG.md` has a section for `0.2.2`, which was never published; the test only accepts published versions or the next one (`0.3.0`). Its entry ("Recompiled template") moves into `0.3.0`.
- `Set-AVMModule`, like the CI's README test, generates this module's README without the "Cross-referenced modules" section, so the committed README never matched. The README is committed as generated. The cross-reference cache records the module's `secrets.bicep` instead of `main.bicep`, which looks like a tooling issue for modules with more than one Bicep file at the root.

### Versioning

`version.json` stays `0.3`, which #6995 set and which was never published; this PR's changes are added to the `0.3.0` CHANGELOG entry. Compared with the published `0.2.1`, `0.3.0` has the same parameters, types and outputs plus the optional `authorizedIPRanges`, and keeps `provisionedClusterInstances` on `2024-01-01`.

### Validation

- `Set-AVMModule` regenerated `main.json` and the README; running it again with fresh caches produces no changes.
- The module workflow ran on this branch with static validation ([run 36866536853](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/actions/runs/36866536853)): 100 static tests passed, including the two that fail on `main`, and all PSRule checks passed.
- This change resolves the three `use-recent-api-versions` warnings on `main`. The remaining `BCP318` warning (the conditional `secrets` module's output) is unchanged from `main`.
- Validated end-to-end on Azure Local, based on the module's `waf-aligned` test: new AKS Arc clusters were created with the updated module through its Key Vault path. The module created the connected cluster through `connected-cluster` `0.3.0` and generated the SSH key pair into the Key Vault, and the cluster uses that key. The deployments used `2024-01-01` for the provisioned cluster instance, `2026-05-01` for the connected cluster and `2026-02-01` for the Key Vault secrets. Re-deployments changed nothing, including the SSH key, also when the key script ran again and read the existing key.

Preserve and extend the existing unreleased changelog section. CI calculates the patch version; release tagging and registry publishing still depend on successful normal validation workflows. This change does not itself publish a release.

As explicitly requested, move only the max test's `enforcedLocation` from `eastus` to `eastasia`. Keep `GP_Gen5`, `Gen5`, `GeneralPurpose`, 4 vCores and all other sizing/region settings unchanged; no ignore files are added.

Make the SQL MI instance name in all four end-to-end scenarios subscription/resource-group-aware: `${namePrefix}-${serviceShort}-${uniqueString(resourceGroup.id)}`. [SQL MI instance names have global scope](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-resource-manager/management/resource-name-rules#microsoftsql), so different test subscriptions must not deliberately reuse the same fixed instance name. The suffix uses the full resource-group ID, including the selected subscription. It stays stable for retries and the serial init/idem pair; it does not depend on deployment name, iteration, run ID or fresh randomness. Only the instance names and generated README examples change. Shared name-prefix tokens, dependency names, module deployment names, batch size, resource settings, parent module source/JSON/version, cleanup ownership and concurrency keys are unchanged by this follow-up. The changelog is preserved; BCPNFR22 does not require entries for test-only changes.

Restore bounded deployment retries for Azure's longer terminal-failure format: `failed with error(s). Showing 1 out of 1 error(s). Status Message: ... (Code: DeploymentFailed)`, including nested `ProvisioningDisabled` quota details. Classification still requires the current deployment name and the first error code in the failure summary. The older short format remains supported. Attempt limits, cleanup ownership, fixed parameters and existing transport, cancellation and unknown-outcome safeguards remain intact. Confirmed quota failures retry in the same region and subscription.

Recover typed HTTP request timeouts after submission by observing the original named deployment in its existing context, not by submitting a replacement. Use the appropriate read-only deployment cmdlet for resource-group, subscription, management-group and tenant scopes. Poll recognized in-progress states every 15 seconds for at most 60 minutes, stopping after three consecutive status-read timeouts. Confirmed success returns the normal outputs; only an observed Failed state enters the existing bounded deployment retry path. Recovered failures retain Azure's operation/provider error details and the original timeout. Failed diagnostic reads remain explicit failures with attempted names retained for cleanup. Authentication/transport errors, missing or ambiguous records, mismatched names, unknown states and exhausted recovery bounds do not permit resubmission. Genuine cancellation and PipelineStopped remain terminal. No workflow timeout settings, global HTTP configuration, SDK internals or cleanup authentication behavior are changed.

Move concurrency controls to the actual deployment and publication jobs, without changing trigger events, label gates or the dispatcher:

- Preselect subscriptions in the `avm-validation` environment using the existing variable/secret precedence, seeded shuffle, round-robin distribution and singleton fallback. Cross-job records carry the original pool index and SHA-256 digest of the canonical subscription GUID, never raw secret-backed identifiers or names. Variable-backed pools show their friendly names; secret-backed configurations show a generic subscription label.
- Before login, resolve exactly the preselected record and verify its ID digest. A changed record fails explicitly rather than selecting another subscription. Reuse that subscription through validation, deployment and cleanup.
- Every actual deployment holds the same module-plus-subscription inner lock through cleanup, independent of branch or shared-scope classification. Management-group, tenant and unresolved linked-template cases also take a distinct per-module outer lock, one test at a time. This preserves exclusion when different revisions add, remove or ignore a shared-scope test, without nested same-key deadlocks. Ordinary and ignored outer calls use unique run/attempt/module/test groups rather than the shared lock.
- Static and PSRule checks remain outside deployment locks. Publication and release-tag jobs retain a separate global per-module lock across legacy, preview, manual and publish-only entry points. All queues use `queue: max`; no active Azure work is automatically cancelled. Legacy entry workflows retain their existing outer scheduling.

Local verification for the naming follow-up: all four end-to-end scenarios compile with Bicep 0.47.16, and all 31 selected existing test-template static checks pass. Compiled-expression assertions confirm the full subscription/resource-group identity and identical instance names across init/idem, with serial batch size 1 unchanged. Native local Bicep evaluation confirms deterministic suffixes, changed suffixes for a different subscription or resource group, and valid 26-character names for every scenario using the configured `gci` prefix. Exact source comparison confirms the instance-name line is the only change in each test. The README was regenerated via dot-sourced `Set-AVMModule -SkipBuild -SkipFileAndFolderSetup`; the parent Bicep/JSON, version, changelog, utilities and workflows are unchanged by this follow-up.

The preceding timeout/concurrency follow-ups passed 690 targeted Pester cases: all 641 previous cases, including the original 191 retry/cleanup/regional regressions, plus 49 timeout-recovery cases. Coverage includes all four scopes, successful recovery with exactly one submission, bounded polling and status-read failures, cancellation, retained provider diagnostics, DoNotThrow, WhatIf, actual cleanup ownership, configuration precedence and secret-safe outputs, pre-login identity failures, cross-revision lock stability, every deployment caller, cleanup lock lifetime, fork isolation and unchanged trigger/manual-publication gates. All Azure interactions in these tests are mocked. Production helper analysis and whitespace checks passed.

The preceding SQL MI/concurrency changes also passed all 28 selected SQL MI static checks, including the original 17 description/ARM/changelog/version checks. The four real SQL MI matrix records were compiled and compared field-for-field against published commit `444e3c8`; the inner lock keys are exactly compatible and unchanged by subsequent follow-ups. Mixed-scope templates were also compiled locally. Actionlint passed with only its unsupported `queue` property diagnostic excluded; `queue: max` is documented GitHub syntax and separately asserted by the workflow tests. Existing Bicep API-age warnings remain in unchanged resources/dependencies.

## Summary

- Coordinate validation and deployment with at most **three distinct region candidates and three deployment attempts total**, rather than multiplying deployment retries by region.
- Allow an automatically selected test location to change after a deployment-stage regional failure only when the exact original deployment is authoritatively `Failed`, every structured error is regional, and its partial resources and deployment records are confirmed removed.
- Preserve existing safe same-region retries, timeout observation without resubmission, cancellation, pinned locations, global/resource-group-scoped tests, resource retention, fixed parameters and timestamps.
- Discover all deployment-operation pages, restore cross-subscription context, confirm supported soft-delete cleanup, remove child records before roots, and keep accurate outstanding cleanup names when cleanup only partly succeeds.
- Preserve original error records while redacting displayed parameter values, restore location-token files on failure, and reject invalid deployment-name prefixes instead of looping indefinitely.

This addresses the [deployment-stage VMSS capacity incident](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/actions/runs/37110850292/job/111168628271), including the nested `InvalidTemplateDeployment` / `SkuNotAvailable` message without a top-level `DeploymentFailed` marker, and structured `ResourceDeploymentFailure` wrappers. `RequestDisallowedByAzure` with the documented `locationineligible` link remains eligible. Unknown/empty codes, unsupported-zone errors, mixed errors, authorization, quota and configuration errors do not authorize relocation.

## Scope

Independent infrastructure change based on `main`; **no `avm/` module files or READMEs changed**. Tests use synthetic templates and a synthetic provider/module identifier, not named AVM modules. Test-location changes remain in companion [#7374](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/pull/7374). Subscription-feature registration is out of scope.

The existing `deploy_step` now performs validation and deployment together. Post-deployment checks and final-cleanup conditions remain unchanged. `removeDeployment=false` disables intermediate cleanup and deployment-stage relocation.

## Local verification

- `Test-TemplateDeploymentWithRetry.Tests.ps1`

All 15 changed PowerShell files and nine action PowerShell blocks parse successfully (after substituting workflow expressions). The nine production PowerShell files have zero PSScriptAnalyzer warning/error findings. `git diff --check` passes.

**Mocked/offline verification only.** No Azure deployments, cloud mutations, workflow reruns, merges, or deployment-triggering labels were performed. Incomplete discovery, uncertain state, reserved soft-deleted resources, or unconfirmed removal stops relocation and preserves remaining cleanup tracking.

## Description

Adds optional Azure subscription feature registration before Bicep deployment tests. The deployment action reads a repository-root `.required-features.json` map from exact module paths to Terraform-compatible `"Namespace/FeatureName"` string arrays:

```json
{
  "avm/res/example/module": ["Microsoft.Example/FeatureOne"]
}
```

The entire map is validated before Azure calls. Missing files, missing exact keys and empty arrays are explicitly logged and skipped. Requirements are not inherited by parent or child modules. Duplicate keys/features, malformed arrays and invalid required values fail explicitly.

Registration runs after Azure login and before token replacement/validation, using the selected test subscription and the effective login tenant. It never switches accounts and verifies the Azure CLI context before making subscription-scoped calls. Static-only and ignored tests do not register features.

Behavior follows the existing Terraform implementation: skip `Registered`, register `NotRegistered`/`Unregistered`, wait without resubmitting `Registering`, then re-register and wait for the provider after each newly completed feature. Defaults are 60 checks with 10-second intervals and a 60-second command timeout. Approval requirements, unexpected states, authorization failures, malformed responses, cancellation and timeouts fail the gate. Registrations persist; nothing is unregistered.

Terraform source: [registration](https://github.com/Azure/azure-verified-modules-tools/blob/b0ba22f2fca81e4e068414e7f20bb703acd37de4/src/Avm.Authoring/Public/Register-AvmFeature.ps1), [manifest parsing](https://github.com/Azure/azure-verified-modules-tools/blob/b0ba22f2fca81e4e068414e7f20bb703acd37de4/src/Avm.Authoring/Private/Features/Read-AvmRequiredFeature.ps1), and [polling](https://github.com/Azure/azure-verified-modules-tools/blob/b0ba22f2fca81e4e068414e7f20bb703acd37de4/src/Avm.Authoring/Private/Features/Wait-AvmAzureRegistration.ps1).

This is an independent change from `main`. It deliberately does **not** create the root map or change any modules; the initial declaration belongs to [#7374](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/pull/7374). Retry/cleanup code and shared environment setup are unchanged. No new dependencies are introduced. The test identity needs `Microsoft.Features/*` and the relevant provider `/register/action` permissions.

All new fixtures use synthetic module paths/features with mocked Azure commands and native processes. No live registrations, deployments, workflow reruns or deployment labels were used.

The [observed deployment job](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/actions/runs/37125785895/job/111211227311) stopped after its first attempt because `Get-ErrorMessageForScope -AsObject` tried to parse the Az operation cmdlet's `StatusMessage` as JSON. Independent main-based follow-up for the nine modules outside the live diff of [#7374](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/pull/7374). **Deployment prerequisite:** provider registration and the corresponding tenant service principals must already exist. Read-only queries by application ID found all three absent from the current CI tenant. This change deliberately does not create them or register providers. The CI identity's Directory Readers access is an agreed prerequisite. No directory roles, app permissions, service principals, or secrets were added.
