## Description

Releases the `avm/res/azure-stack-hci/virtual-machine-instance` changes from #7429, which were merged but never published, as `0.3.0`. MCR's latest version is still `0.1.2`.

### Why `0.2.0` was never published

- After #7429 merged, the module pipeline on `main` failed the static test "Set-ModuleReadMe script should not apply any updates": the README's cross-reference to `avm/res/hybrid-compute/machine` was out of date.
- #7430 fixed the README. README-only changes don't trigger the module pipeline, and a manual run on `main` then passed all checks but skipped tag creation, because a release is only created when the last commit changes `main.json` or `version.json`.

### This PR

- `version.json`: `0.2` → `0.3`.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: renames the unpublished `## 0.2.0` section to `## 0.3.0`, with the same changes and a note that `0.2.0` was never published.

There are no template changes: `main.bicep`, `main.json` and the README are unchanged, and running `Set-AVMModule` with fresh caches produces no changes.

## Description

<!--
>Thank you for your contribution !
> Please include a summary of the change and which issue is fixed.
> Please also include the context.
> List any dependencies that are required for this change.

Fixes #123
Closes #123
-->

Repair shared cleanup and retry failures observed in [run 37438688587](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/actions/runs/37438688587), retaining the original narrowly qualified missing-child preflight fix.

This is the consolidated tooling review: it includes the Cosmos classifier from [#7465](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/pull/7465), the AKS classifier from [#7467](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/pull/7467), and the complete twelve-file non-`avm/` slice from [#7374](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/pull/7374), including its held Image Builder repair. All twelve transferred blobs exactly match source commit `3eb4712cdcc89d6b50a8069f080bb1cca9d09f00`; there were no source-content deviations. The module source branch was not merged into this history. There are no `avm/` differences from main `956e47dc71e85e0c8307edd4fc70418b14c840c8`.

- **Missing preflight child:** only a failed parent's unique failed Create with matching direct preflight evidence and an exact child-record `404 DeploymentNotFound` permits omission. Successful siblings and owned resources still require cleanup.
- **Existing Graph lookup:** an ID-less successful Create is omitted from resource deletion only when that exact deployment's server-exported template proves a literal `existing: true` service-principal declaration. Symbol, type, import alias, provider and version must match uniquely. Missing export access, malformed/duplicate metadata and unproven declarations block strict cleanup; parent proof is never reused for a child.
- **Asynchronous history deletion:** after an accepted DELETE, confirm absence with at most three exact-record GETs, 15 seconds apart only while a terminal record remains visible. Preserve pending root ownership for final cleanup instead of rediscovering an already-deleted root for 39 minutes. Do not repeat DELETE or claim removal before confirmation.
- **ACI capacity:** recognize only the captured documented, message-only capacity leaf for a current-subscription container group in the selected location, with a standard-size Linux request. Generic messages, explicit unknown/empty codes, quota and mixed failures remain ineligible.
- **ML workspace Cosmos capacity:** retain the exact structured workspace failure and embedded Cosmos high-demand response, requiring the named region to match the selected location. Generic `BadRequest`, region-access/quota guesses, malformed payloads and mixed errors do not qualify.
- **AKS empty-zone preflight:** retain the exact managed-cluster preflight response where supported zones are explicitly empty in the selected region. General unsupported-zone messages, a different region, ambiguous metadata and mixed errors remain ineligible.
- **Intentional same-region exception:** add a new, narrowly supported transient-deployment path, rather than classifying generic HTTP 500 as regional. Every error leaf must be `InternalServerError` under a matching resource failure for `Microsoft.Network/applicationGateways`, `Microsoft.DBforPostgreSQL/flexibleServers` or `Microsoft.Network/privateEndpoints`. Require the exact Failed root, complete terminal discovery, **no deployment scripts anywhere in the discovered attempt**, and verified resource/history removal before replay. Validation-stage 500, mixed/unknown/auth failures, unsupported targets, pins, global or resource-group scope, retained resources and ambiguous/nonterminal roots do not enable this path.

Original errors, remaining deployment names, context restoration and the three-region/three-submission limits are preserved. Mixed regional/transient attempts revalidate only when changing regions. No `avm/` fixtures, public module APIs, package dependencies or broad unsupported-region/zone/quota rules are changed.

### Transferred tooling

- Image Builder startup waits for the newly submitted run, not an earlier success or the completion of the run request. Waiting is bounded by the build timeout plus five minutes; explicit asynchronous mode remains supported. VHD copying requires a successful build, waits up to five minutes for one valid output, resolves one source/destination storage context, and checks a requested completed copy.
- The replication-region helper selects a provider-supported secondary region, preferring the paired region before deterministic recommendation/geography fallbacks. The FinOps Hub workflow exposes its existing location override as an optional dispatch input.
- `.required-features.json` declares the VMSS `Microsoft.Compute/EncryptionAtHost` prerequisite for the existing deployment-only registration path. No feature was registered during this work.
- Agent setup registers the default PowerShell Gallery only when absent, respecting `ShouldProcess` and surfacing discovery/registration failures.
- README generation preserves quoted values and URLs when stripping inline comments, prefers canonical resource metadata, and retains explicit failure for malformed metadata.
- Static PSRule analysis preserves the shared `builtInServicePrincipalObjectId` placeholder `00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001`. The HCI prerequisite helper uses Key Vault API `2026-02-01` for its vault and five secrets without changing its RBAC setting.

**Remaining limitation:** the captured Application Gateway WAF and managed-environment max failures include deployment scripts, so they remain ineligible for the new same-region replay path. Resource/history absence does not prove delayed script deletion work has finished. Their provider failures still need a future authorized run; this change does not claim they are repaired. Graph omission also remains conditional on successful exact-template export. No live Azure validation was performed.

### Validation

Offline reproductions failed before the corresponding shared repairs: 17 history-removal cases, 17 Graph-proof cases, four transient-eligibility controls, and five script-replay/root-state controls. The consolidated run passed **1,521 tests, 0 failed, 0 skipped, 0 not run**. This includes all **1,353 tests in the nine requested suites**:

| Suite | Passed |
| --- | ---: |
| `Invoke-TemplateDeploymentWithRetry.Tests.ps1` | 479 |
| `DeploymentCleanupWorkflow.Tests.ps1` | 149 |
| `Test-TemplateDeploymentWithRetry.Tests.ps1` | 365 |
| `RegionalValidationWorkflow.Tests.ps1` | 21 |
| `CIParameterWorkflow.Tests.ps1` | 11 |
| `ModuleWorkflow.Tests.ps1` | 253 |
| `ImageBuilderScripts.Tests.ps1` | 53 |
| `ModuleReadMeStaticValidation.Tests.ps1` | 16 |
| `Set-EnvironmentOnAgent.Tests.ps1` | 6 |

Additional relevant coverage passed **168 tests**:

| Suite | Passed |
| --- | ---: |
| `Set-ModuleReadme.Tests.ps1` | 4 |
| `ModuleReadMeNotices.Tests.ps1` | 5 |
| `Register-RequiredSubscriptionFeature.Tests.ps1` | 134 |
| `RequiredSubscriptionFeaturesWorkflow.Tests.ps1` | 8 |
| Private `ConsolidatedToolingHelpers.Tests.ps1` | 17 |

The private supplemental fixture checks paired/fallback region selection, rejection and error propagation, FinOps input forwarding, the exact feature map and static GUID. It is retained with the validation reports, not added to the transferred source slice. Azure calls and repository registration are mocked; process TEMP/TMP is isolated.

Executed test inputs and commands follow. `$artifacts` is the private validation artifact directory containing the supplemental fixture; only its machine-specific value is omitted.

Result: **passed, 1,521/1,521**. All added tests from both classifier inputs survive. The Graph predicate also matched the three supplied full CI-compiled fixture templates (Linux max, Windows max and WAF).

```powershell

Result: **passed, 64/64**, including all **18 generic InternalServerError regional-negative controls**. `$replayHarness` is the coordinator's private captured-error harness. The adapter loads the actual shared classifier helper and obtains subscription context only from each exact captured root deployment ID; it changes none of the 64 assertions or expectations.

```powershell

$paths = @(
    '.\utilities\pipelines\e2eValidation\resourceDeployment\Invoke-TemplateDeploymentWithRetry.ps1'

The README helper also emits one pre-existing unmatched `ResourceTypesToExclude` suppression diagnostic; it occurs in both the destination baseline and frozen source. ## Description

<!--
>Thank you for your contribution !
> Please include a summary of the change and which issue is fixed.
> Please also include the context.
> List any dependencies that are required for this change.

Fixes #123
Closes #123
-->

Recognize the observed AKS managed-cluster preflight capacity failure in the shared regional retry classifier. Azure can report `InvalidTemplateDeployment` with an `AvailabilityZoneNotSupported` detail when valid requested zones have an empty supported-zone set in the selected region.

This layer depends on the selected-resource-location classifier context in [#7465](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/pull/7465). Its base is `jaredfholgate-cosmos-regional-retries` at `26bfe9db80512be270ad4e541a9392432c4ec0a1`; the sole new commit is `924c62c6a14c25e855007f6c054b938250e4b4d4`. Fixture-delivery changes remain separate in [#7374](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/pull/7374). No Bicep, README, version or deployment-fixture files change here.

Recognition requires the genuine error code, the immediate complete `Microsoft.ContainerService/managedClusters` preflight message, distinct valid requested Azure zones (`1`, `2`, `3`), an empty supported-zone set, and the exact selected resource location after canonical/display-name normalization. The sanitized fixture preserves the captured nested ARM deployment envelope without inventing a cluster resource-ID target.

Malformed/trailing or duplicate JSON, missing/mismatched locations, unrelated providers, nonempty supported zones, unknown/mixed/contradictory error trees, quota/authentication/authorization/cancellation evidence, and the separate `PropertyChangeNotAllowed` API-version failure remain nonregional. The parser deliberately fails closed on other preflight formats.

Assessed revision: `151a685c2f264b0a81dfc25d49859dc7adf97b90` | Dimension | Assessment | Rationale | |---|---|---| | Change confidence | 8.5/10 | ↑ Preceding head `7bce41654` passed all 24/24 static/unit checks and 20/20 required E2E deployments twice ([run 45473278125](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/actions/runs/45473278125) and [run 45505059776](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/actions/runs/45505059776/attempts/2)).
↑ `151a685c2` adds only `service_privateEndpoints` `dependsOn` sequencing after the 14 APIM child module collections, the `portalsetting` `validationSecondaryKey` `@description` clarification, and a unit test; local `Invoke-AvmPrCheck`, `Invoke-AvmTestUnit`, `prettier:check`, and full cross-family review (`claude-sonnet-5.5`) passed with zero findings.
↓ Hosted required E2E on `151a685c2` is pending to confirm clean deployment and whether child-module sequencing reduces the APIM `waf-aligned` Private Endpoint `InternalServerError` → `ServiceLocked` flake. | | Diagnosis confidence | 9/10 | ↑ Pinned compiler comparisons establish the original plain-boundary forwarding gaps across all modified parent and child entrypoints.
↑ Logs from `45505059776` and `45509719072` confirm `service_privateEndpoints` launched concurrently with APIM child deployments before failing with `InternalServerError` and an immediate `ServiceLocked` retry, though sequencing does not prove concurrency caused the RP `InternalServerError`.
↓ APIM provider first-create behavior and optional Integration `max` `KeyVaultOperationFailed` (#7607) remain outside this PR's contract scope. | | Evidence fit | 8/10 | ↑ Reproduced compiler diagnostics match the credential-boundary hardening target across parent and child modules.
↓ These diagnostics establish compile-time and ARM-boundary protection rather than an observed credential exposure or runtime secrecy guarantee. | ## Description This is defense-in-depth hardening for credential inputs across **89 changed files in 12 parent modules and 6 child modules**. A secure child parameter does not protect a value at a plain parent boundary, and secure parent values can lose their protection when forwarded to ordinary child inputs. The changes preserve secure typing across those boundaries without changing resource assignments. Current head `151a685c2` incorporates `main` (`abbc773d5`, including #7374, #7608, #7644, and #7527), clarifies `portalsetting`'s `validationSecondaryKey` description as a defensive secure pass-through, sequences `api-management/service` `service_privateEndpoints` after all 14 APIM child module collections so Private Link writes do not overlap concurrent APIM subresource updates, and keeps out-of-scope fixture edits and redundant schema-restating unit tests trimmed. Fixes #7646. Fixes #7648. Fixes #7503 (the `fluxConfigurations` description typo in `kubernetes-configuration/extension`, included because that parameter declaration is updated here). ### Why this PR was reworked Validation uses the merged Bicep rules `use-secure-value-for-secure-inputs` and `no-secure-values-in-insecure-inputs` ([Azure/bicep#20520](https://github.com/Azure/bicep/pull/20520), [Azure/bicep#20553](https://github.com/Azure/bicep/pull/20553)), not a custom PowerShell forwarding analyzer. The original hardening removes 17 production forwarding warnings, and its stronger contracts exposed 17 test-caller warnings that are addressed here without changing sample data or suppressing secret-leak checks. Integration Account assembly content and Web site/slot config boundaries are included because they share the same direct parent-to-child forwarding gap. **Reconciliation of the original 17 at `aa13902bd`:** running the pinned compiler (`Bicep v0.49.22` source base `6f783fb4a046fafc618c76ec258c8092bd7b249e` plus v4 patch SHA256 `9828ed9516d75d2c15a9906e3f5de57507053ec784538ff03a46d5a2fe80efcc`) on the original 11 production entrypoints compared `main` `4962ab5a9` against `aa13902bd`: `main` had **47 secure-rule occurrences / 43 unique fingerprints**, and the PR had **26 unique fingerprints** (26 common in preexisting VM/VMSS DSC siblings, 17 `main`-only resolved here, and zero PR-only). | Original production finding | Count | Rule | | --- | ---: | --- | | `api-management/service/main.bicep`: `value`, `primaryKey`, `secondaryKey`; `properties.validationKey` | 4 | Three `use-secure-value-for-secure-inputs`; one `no-secure-values-in-insecure-inputs` | | `api-management/service/workspace/main.bicep`: `credentials.*`, `value`, `primaryKey`, `secondaryKey` | 4 | `use-secure-value-for-secure-inputs` | | `app/managed-environment/main.bicep`: `certificateValue` | 1 | `use-secure-value-for-secure-inputs` | | `automation/automation-account/main.bicep`: `value` | 1 | `use-secure-value-for-secure-inputs` | | `compute/virtual-machine-scale-set/main.bicep`: `protectedSettings` | 1 | `use-secure-value-for-secure-inputs` | | `compute/virtual-machine/main.bicep`: `protectedSettings` | 1 | `use-secure-value-for-secure-inputs` | | `container-registry/registry/main.bicep`: `serviceUri` | 1 | `use-secure-value-for-secure-inputs` | | `container-service/managed-cluster/main.bicep`: `configurationProtectedSettings.*` | 1 | `use-secure-value-for-secure-inputs` | | `key-vault/vault/main.bicep`: `contentType` | 1 | `use-secure-value-for-secure-inputs` | | `kubernetes-configuration/extension/main.bicep`: `configurationProtectedSettings.*` | 1 | `use-secure-value-for-secure-inputs` | | `sql/server/main.bicep`: `storageAccountAccessKey` | 1 | `use-secure-value-for-secure-inputs` | ### Credential boundaries | Module | Next version | Secured inputs | | --- | --- | --- | | `api-management/service` (`cache` `0.1.3`, `portalsetting` `0.2.0`, `workspace` `0.1.1`) | `0.16.0` | Cache connection strings, subscription keys, generated named-value fallback, workspace credentials/named values, parent delegation `validationKey`, and both validation-key leaves in the existing open child pass-through | | `app/managed-environment` | `0.17.1` | Certificate content | | `automation/automation-account` | `0.20.0` | Variable values | | `compute/virtual-machine` and `compute/virtual-machine-scale-set` | `0.23.0` / `0.12.0` | DSC protected settings | | `container-registry/registry` | `0.13.3` | Webhook service URI | | `container-service/managed-cluster` | `0.14.2` | Extension protected configuration | | `key-vault/vault` | `0.14.4` | Secret content type, matching its child contract | | `kubernetes-configuration/extension` | `0.4.0` | Flux protected configuration; description typo | | `logic/integration-account` | `0.2.2` | Assembly content | | `sql/server` | `0.23.2` | Security-alert-policy storage account access keys | | `web/site` (`config` `0.2.3`, `slot` `0.5.1`, `slot/config` `0.1.1`) | `0.24.1` | Config properties, retained app settings, credential dictionary leaves, connection strings/SAS URLs, storage-key fixture outputs | Web config shapes overlap and permit arbitrary keys; a leaf-discriminated union would change the caller interface. Both child config parameters are secure objects. Two documented parent forwarding exceptions cover only `use-secure-value-for-secure-inputs` on mixed properties, not `no-secure-values-in-insecure-inputs`. Parent contracts protect 21 credential paths while keeping ordinary names and flags ordinary. The APIM fallback retains `newGuid()` behind a secure boundary, and workspace logger credentials retain their resource-derived shape and optionality. ### Native types and compatibility [d33eef811](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/commit/d33eef811cea7a495126cd6c920213c834a90b08) addresses Alex's [native-type question](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/pull/7472#discussion_r4478700797). Stock Bicep emits the portal `resourceInput<...>.properties` projection as a generic object with resource-derived metadata; projecting individual fields produces `BCP052`, while intersections, type spread, and an override argument are unsupported (`BCP001`, `BCP317`, `BCP071`). Securing the whole native parameter compiles but unnecessarily protects ordinary siblings. The portal-setting child UDT maintains only secure nullable `validationKey` and `validationSecondaryKey`, plus `*: any`, rather than copying the provider variant schema. The old undiscriminated `resourceInput<...>.properties` projection already accepted arbitrary fields; the child change constrains those two existing pass-through leaves to string/null and protects them while leaving ordinary and future siblings open. Automation similarly constrains only secure `value`; VM/VMSS constrain only secure `protectedSettings`; Flux reuses provider field types and leaves other fields open. The parent advertises only the documented `validationKey`. [3fef54e85](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/commit/3fef54e8575f30e99c89dd44ce8842b8973c7cb9) removed the temporary parent `validationSecondaryKey` declaration after full-diff review confirmed that both the [2024-05-01 ARM reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/templates/microsoft.apimanagement/2024-05-01/service/portalsettings) and [REST create/update reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/apimanagement/delegation-settings/create-or-update?view=rest-apimanagement-2024-05-01) document only the primary key. [4377789d8](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/commit/4377789d8c7575a4e61d4326c25feac773b1c688) makes `namespace`, `scope`, and `kustomizations` required native projections in `fluxConfigurationType` to match this wrapper's direct reads and the published `flux-configuration:0.3.8` child's required inputs. | Contract | Preserved | New restriction versus `main` | | --- | --- | --- | | Portal `properties` | Required root/no default; ordinary/future siblings; absent/null key | Non-string, non-null `validationKey` or `validationSecondaryKey` rejected | | Automation `variables` | `[]` default; string values including serialized examples; ordinary sibling types; extra fields | Object entries containing string `value` required; scalar, missing-value, and non-string-value cases newly rejected | | VM/VMSS DSC | Ordinary root; `{ enabled: false }` default; `{}`; unconstrained ordinary siblings/unknown fields; absent/null protected settings | Non-object, non-null `protectedSettings` rejected | | Flux configurations | Nullable outer array; empty array; native field-type reuse; open `name`/unknown fields; secure optional protected settings; unchanged forwarding | Missing `namespace`, `scope`, or `kustomizations` now causes stock `BCP035` errors, and explicit ARM schemas add parameter-file validation | Because these modules are pre-1.0, SNFR17 uses **minor** version bumps for the breaking validation narrowings (`api-management/service/portalsetting` `0.2.0` → `api-management/service` `0.16.0`, `automation/automation-account` `0.20.0`, `compute/virtual-machine` `0.23.0`, `compute/virtual-machine-scale-set` `0.12.0`, `kubernetes-configuration/extension` `0.4.0`). ### Fixtures, generation, and `main` merge reconciliation Credential examples use secure test inputs, and verified public fixtures use optional secure parameters with unchanged defaults and narrow explained `secure-parameter-default` directives outside README-extracted blocks. Merging `main` (`abbc773d5`) brings in #7374, #7608, #7644, and #7527, and all 18 modified modules (`12` parents + `6` modified children) are generated cleanly via `Avm.Authoring` (`bicep 0.49.2`). Five open wildcard entries (`>Any_other_property<`) emit `- Type: ` with a trailing space from canonical `Invoke-AvmDocs`; `.prettierignore` excludes `avm/` and `Invoke-AvmPrCheck`'s `docs` step enforces canonical `Invoke-AvmDocs` output. Secure decorators do not hide template literals, protect an upstream plain parameter, or erase historical deployment values. ### Companion PRs merged to unblock CI and validation Driving this PR to green exposed pre-existing module, fixture, authoring-tool, and compiler issues that we split out and merged separately so `#7472` stays scoped to credential boundaries: - **Registry CI, metadata, and E2E fixtures (`Azure/bicep-registry-modules`):** - #7493 — Fixed a `Microsoft.ApiManagement/service/namesValues` `canonicalType` typo in `named-value/metadata.json` that broke APIM `README.md` parity checks. - #7601 — Fixed `dns-resolver` `forwardingRuleType.metadata` (`string?` vs `object?`) exposed by the repository-wide Bicep type-inference scan. - #7602 — Fixed `synapse/workspace` Big Data Pool required/nullable forwarding and output casing exposed by the same scan. - #7609 — Switched `container-registry/registry` E2E fixtures to the service-aware replication-region helper so Geo-Replication stops picking unsupported paired regions (closed #7606). - #7608 — Corrected `api-management/service` `v2max` subnet delegation from `Microsoft.Web/serverFarms` to `Microsoft.ApiManagement/service` (closed #7605). - #7527 — Replaced disallowed `Standard_DS2_v2` AKS node sizing, pinned `swedencentral`, dropped the retired Flux `0.5.2` version pin (`releaseTrain: 'stable'`), updated `connected-cluster` off preview AKS APIs, and registered `Microsoft.Kubernetes` for `kubernetes-configuration/extension` E2E tests (closed #7526). - **AVM CI and authoring tooling (`Azure/azure-verified-modules-tools`):** - [Azure/azure-verified-modules-tools#354](https://github.com/Azure/azure-verified-modules-tools/pull/354) — Masked nested `Microsoft.Resources/deployments` `_generator` metadata so `avm.bicep.json-stale` stops failing on compiler-version provenance drift ([Azure/azure-verified-modules-tools#353](https://github.com/Azure/azure-verified-modules-tools/issues/353)). - review_comments.body:
Hey @andyleejordan,
overall a great contribution, thank you 💪 Just two asks in alignment with the contribution guidelines: Please run the tests for all updated workflows & attach their workflow badge.
You can make this very simple by just invoking the [Invoke-WorkflowsForBranch](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/blob/main/utilities/tools/Invoke-WorkflowsForBranch.ps1) function with the `WorkflowInputs` parameter specified as `-WorkflowInputs @{ staticValidation = 'true'; deploymentValidation = 'true'; removeDeployment = 'true' }`.
The function will automatically return the workflow badges to you as markdown which you can then copy into the PR description.

For trivia: The reason why this is important is to ensure we only merge changes that will pass the tests in `main`. If they'd not, the version of the code in the repository would diverge from the one published, making it hard to understand what was and wasn't already published + if a bug were to be introduced, any other contributor would need to fix it first before they could contribute to an impacted module. :)

## Description

<!--
>Thank you for your contribution !
> Please include a summary of the change and which issue is fixed.
> Please also include the context.
> List any dependencies that are required for this change.

Fixes #123
Closes #123
-->

Recover a successful management-group deployment when the submission command reports HTTP 403 after Azure has completed the original deployment. The observed failure was a successful root deployment followed by a client-side authorization error; repeating the template with a new deployment name can create another set of resources.

This tooling-only change:
- Recognizes explicit HTTP 403 status evidence through exception wrappers, while keeping cancellation terminal.
- Uses the original submission's Azure context, deployment name and management group, and verifies the returned full deployment resource ID.
- Reuses bounded observation of the original deployment and returns its outputs only for confirmed `Succeeded`. Active states retain the existing 60-minute observation window and status-read timeouts retain their three-consecutive-timeout bound.
- Preserves original error records/details and fails closed for failed, cancelled, unknown, missing, mismatched or inaccessible results. Further HTTP 403 status reads are not retried.
- Leaves regional/submission budgets and cleanup policy unchanged. No module files, permissions or workflow definitions change.

**Deliberately excluded:** replay of genuinely failed HTTP 403 deployments, including same-name replay. HTTP 403 alone does not establish permission propagation, and the incident supports successful-result reconciliation rather than retrying a failed deployment. No deployment, Azure write, permission change or workflow rerun was performed. No new dependencies are required.

## Description

<!--
>Thank you for your contribution !
> Please include a summary of the change and which issue is fixed.
> Please also include the context.
> List any dependencies that are required for this change.

Fixes #123
Closes #123
-->

Repairs two shared cleanup response contracts without changing regional retry budgets or deployment policy:

- Read deployment operations with ARM API `2025-04-01`. The older API omits the resource type and extension metadata of an existing Graph lookup, causing the existing strict completeness check to reject an otherwise terminal deployment. Pagination, exact scope checks, terminal-state checks and the exact exported-template proof remain required.
- After an accepted history deletion, treat an exact matching, correctly shaped HTTP 200 deployment in `Deleting` as still present. Reconcile only within the existing three reads/two 15-second sleeps. Relocation still requires confirmed absence. Normal resource checks do not gain this exception; denials, mismatched identities, contradictory errors and unknown response shapes fail closed.
- Report selected response identity/state/type/error-code fields for rejected cleanup responses, without dumping deployment parameters, outputs or provider error messages. Malformed JSON fails with safe HTTP/resource context.
- Add 27 isolated response-contract regressions and one integrated `Deleting`-to-absence relocation regression. Update only operation-API expectations in the existing workflow fixtures.

**Evidence and limits:** [Incident run](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/actions/runs/37524178586), tested commit `aea7a53ec07cc36522bac7683bb8846a64321abf`. Read-only observations of the same failed VM root confirmed all operations were terminal: API `2021-04-01` returned an ID-less Graph target with only `symbolicName`, while API `2025-04-01` retained `resourceType` and `extension`. The original rejected HTTP 200 bodies from AKS/VMSS history deletion were not logged and cannot now be recovered. This change does **not** establish that those historical responses were `Deleting`; it adds bounded handling for that valid progress shape and diagnostics for other rejected shapes.

Independent of [#7478](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/pull/7478) and [#7437](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/pull/7437), which overlap test files only. Their unmerged implementations are not imported. No changes to `avm/`, `New-TemplateDeployment.ps1`, `Get-DeploymentErrorKind.ps1`, or [#7374](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/pull/7374). All 65 open reviews were checked for intended-path overlap before publication; no duplicate implementation was found. No new dependencies.

**Intentionally unresolved:**

- The source-VHD copy failure remains a real failed deployment. `Copy-VhdToStorageAccount.ps1` is unchanged: the pinned Az.Storage 6.0.0 implementation already reads source metadata and generates source-read authorization for cross-account copying. The incident's Image Builder/staging resources are now absent, so an authentication/readiness/lifetime cause cannot be proved. A further authorized run needs token-free source-read status/error/request IDs near copy submission plus Image Builder/staging lifecycle timestamps before a generic retry or lifetime repair is justified.
- Purge-protected vault reservations remain fail-closed. A safe change needs an explicit region/attempt naming contract with retained-vault ownership accounting, or supported original-region recovery/reuse. Purge protection and retained-resource guards are unchanged.

References: [operation response schema](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/resources/deployment-operations/list-at-subscription-scope?view=rest-resources-2025-04-01), [asynchronous deployment deletion](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/resources/deployments/delete-at-subscription-scope?view=rest-resources-2025-04-01), [pinned copy cmdlet implementation](https://github.com/Azure/azure-powershell/blob/v11.0.0-November2023/src/Storage/Storage/Blob/Cmdlet/StartAzureStorageBlobCopy.cs), [Image Builder VHD lifecycle](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/linux/image-builder-json#distribute-vhd), [vault retention](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/key-vault/general/soft-delete-overview).

## Pipeline Reference

## Description

<!--
>Thank you for your contribution !

> Please also include the context.

Fixes #123
Closes #123
-->

Select Pester through the supported Avm.Authoring public tool contract **before** `New-PesterContainer` or `Invoke-Pester` can autoload a different version.

The inspected VMSS, Log Analytics workspace, and App Configuration static-validation jobs in [automatic run 37600339583](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/actions/runs/37600339583) loaded Pester 5.9.0, then failed nested metadata validation because released Avm.Authoring 0.21.0 selected 5.7.1. This change does not assume that every failed job in that run had the same error.

- Add one shared initializer and call it from full module static validation, the standalone metadata workflow, `Test-ModuleLocally` (`PesterTest` and `PesterTestRecurse` only), and `Test-CI` (whose ownership tests also run nested metadata validation).
- Require **Avm.Authoring 0.21.0 or later**. Version 0.20.0 lacks the managed-Pester/`-Path` contract; an already loaded older release fails with an update/restart instruction rather than being replaced in-process.
- Use `Get-AvmTool` to resolve the configured manifest and `Install-AvmTool -Name Pester` only when it reports the prerequisite missing. Respect disabled auto-install, validate the selected manifest/import, and fail clearly for incompatible loaded engines, invalid resolution, or installation/import errors.
- Preserve repository overrides through the public resolver. No Pester version is hardcoded in consumer logic, no repository pin override is added, and no private Avm.Authoring API or module-removal workaround is used.
- Keep shared metadata validation, test scope/results, deployment behavior, permissions, cleanup, and retry settings unchanged. Local initialization occurs outside the existing test exception handler so initialization errors cannot become successful string output.

This is a consuming-repository fix only; it does not change upstream Avm.Authoring, its strict pin/integrity policy, module sources, or module versions.

Implementation commit: `3cf62c5d934ac4a9bbaa510686bfbea5d7357533`  
Tree: `8cc879b75fac0fb5deb9c6e92328025d0bce089f`  
Main-based parent: `6001a5b529e3e6490c0b63323fb60b9e069ffd9d`

### Local validation

Executed on Windows with PowerShell 7.6.6 and released Avm.Authoring 0.21.0. The conflicting Pester 5.9.0 was absent locally initially; after that missing-dependency failure it was restored with the exact command below, **only into the session directory**, not a user/system module installation:

```powershell

$env:PSModulePath = 'C:\Users\jaredholgate\.copilot\session-state\a4fc419c-db4f-4f4c-ba05-30e5dfa4acbc\files\dependencies' + [IO.Path]::PathSeparator + $env:PSModulePath

#### Actual shared metadata suite, in another fresh process

```powershell

An additional session-local harness (not a repository dependency or committed file) ran ten isolated processes using the actual entry-point scripts:

```powershell

### Local Azure deployment evidence

Tested commit: `6325b9eb7f545a3e9d2f2095ee6847bfbad6ee73`. Region: `swedencentral`. Azure CLI `2.92.0`; Bicep CLI `0.47.16`.

These are real Azure deployments initiated locally, **not a GitHub Actions run**. The module-specific workflow is introduced by this PR. Tests started on 2026-11-13 (UTC); all test resource groups were confirmed absent by 2026-11-14 00:30:19 UTC.

The three existing E2E fixtures were compiled without Bicep source changes. Their generated ARM templates had only `variables.resourceLocation` changed from the hardcoded `eastus2` to `swedencentral`. Unique names were supplied through the existing `namePrefix` and `resourceGroupName` parameters. Dependencies used `Standard_D4s_v7` and `MicrosoftSQLServer:SQL2022-WS2022:sqldev-gen2:latest`.

| Scenario / attempt | Subscription deployment | ARM result | Duration | Module `init` | Module `idem` | Resource group cleanup |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| defaults | `pr7485-s11132333-defaults` | Succeeded | 8m 05s | Succeeded | Succeeded | Confirmed deleted |
| max (first attempt) | `pr7485-s11132333-max` | Failed | 11m 09s | Not reached | Not reached | Confirmed deleted |
| max (retry 1) | `pr7485-s11132333-max-r1` | Failed (subscription policy restriction) | 33m 08s | Failed | Not reached | Confirmed deleted |
| waf-aligned | `pr7485-s11132333-waf-aligned` | Succeeded | 8m 11s | Succeeded | Succeeded | Confirmed deleted |

The first `max` attempt failed in the dependency VM's `MicrosoftAntiMalware` extension with `OperationPreempted` ("Operation execution has been preempted by a more recent operation."), before either SQL module iteration ran. Its resources were deleted before retrying. The single retry used the identical compiled template with fresh resource names. Its VM dependencies succeeded, but the SQL module `init` failed with `Ext_AutomatedBackup_AzureStorageError`: Azure Storage returned HTTP 403, `KeyBasedAuthenticationNotPermitted` ("Key based authentication is not permitted on this storage account."). The fixture requests `allowSharedKeyAccess: true`.

**Confirmed cause of the retry failure: inherited Azure Policy restrictions in the author's test subscription.** Follow-up investigation on 2026-11-19 found successful `Microsoft.Authorization/policies/modify/action` events against this exact backup storage account at 2026-11-13 23:52:22 and 23:52:24 UTC. The applied management-group policy uses `addOrReplace` to force `Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/allowSharedKeyAccess` to `false`, overriding the fixture's explicit `true`. This explains why automated-backup provisioning was rejected with `KeyBasedAuthenticationNotPermitted`: the test environment disallowed the authentication method required by this scenario. The captured failure is therefore attributable to the test subscription's inherited policy restriction, not evidence of a SQL module implementation defect. The `max` scenario still needs a successful end-to-end run in a compatible test environment.

 The `idem` iteration was not reached. No successful max-scenario validation is claimed, and no policy or security controls were weakened to force a pass.

Successful scenarios also returned `Succeeded` for the SQL virtual machine resource. This evidence covers ARM provisioning and the fixtures' repeated module deployment, not functional execution of scheduled backups, assessments, patching, or SQL queries. Pester and PSRule were not rerun as part of this deployment-evidence exercise.

<details>
<summary>Executed commands and verification results</summary>

The commands below omit the private subscription ID and absolute local artifact directory, represented by `$subscriptionId` and `$artifactDir`. The build loop used each scenario's existing `tests\e2e\<scenario>\main.test.bicep` as `$source` and an isolated artifact path as `$compiledPath`.

# Local generated-ARM adaptation only; applied identically to all three templates.
$template.variables.resourceLocation = 'swedencentral'
$template | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 100 | Set-Content -LiteralPath $templatePath -Encoding utf8

# defaults: Succeeded; final state verified separately below.
az deployment sub create --subscription $subscriptionId --location swedencentral --name pr7485-s11132333-defaults --template-file $artifactDir\defaults.swedencentral.json --parameters namePrefix=s11132333 resourceGroupName=avm-pr7485-s11132333-defaults --no-wait --only-show-errors --output none
# max: Failed; final state verified separately below.
az deployment sub create --subscription $subscriptionId --location swedencentral --name pr7485-s11132333-max --template-file $artifactDir\max.swedencentral.json --parameters namePrefix=s11132333 resourceGroupName=avm-pr7485-s11132333-max --no-wait --only-show-errors --output none
# max retry 1: Failed; final state verified separately below.
az deployment sub create --subscription $subscriptionId --location swedencentral --name pr7485-s11132333-max-r1 --template-file $artifactDir\max.swedencentral.json --parameters namePrefix=r11132333 resourceGroupName=avm-pr7485-s11132333-max-r1 --no-wait --only-show-errors --output none
# waf-aligned: Succeeded; final state verified separately below.
az deployment sub create --subscription $subscriptionId --location swedencentral --name pr7485-s11132333-waf-aligned --template-file $artifactDir\waf-aligned.swedencentral.json --parameters namePrefix=s11132333 resourceGroupName=avm-pr7485-s11132333-waf-aligned --no-wait --only-show-errors --output none
```

`--no-wait` only submits a deployment. Completion was checked repeatedly for every deployment name in the table using the following command; the final states are recorded above:

```powershell
az deployment sub show --subscription $subscriptionId --name $deploymentName --query '{state:properties.provisioningState,timestamp:properties.timestamp,duration:properties.duration,error:properties.error,correlationId:properties.correlationId}' --only-show-errors --output json

# init/idem results: both Succeeded for each successful scenario.
az deployment group list --subscription $subscriptionId --resource-group $resourceGroup --query '[].{name:name,state:properties.provisioningState,duration:properties.duration}' --only-show-errors --output json

# After capturing results and removing any test-created resource locks:

az group exists --subscription $subscriptionId --name $resourceGroup --only-show-errors --output json

Only two files change: the existing shared classifier and a focused regression file. There are no module Bicep, metadata, dependency, region-list, or region-pin changes. The three-candidate/three-submission limits, deployment identity, cleanup, permission/cancellation checks, original ErrorRecord, and safe diagnostic redaction are unchanged. **SDK evidence and uncertainty**

The installed Az.Resources 7.4.0 and 9.0.3 assemblies expose `PSResourceManagerError.Code`, `Message`, `Target`, and `Details`. The preserved AKS log does **not** contain the raw SDK response, so this establishes a reproducible SDK-shape defect, not proof that null members were the exact live payload. Display redaction is not the classifier input.

Tooling-only follow-up for two failures in [automatic run 37785195552](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/actions/runs/37785195552), using SDK contracts and offline reproductions rather than replaying deployments.

- **Container Instance cleanup discovery:** individual operation-page GETs and strict scoped status reads can retry an unambiguous typed HttpClient timeout. The limit is three total reads, five seconds apart, without replaying successful pages. Partial output is discarded; exhausted reads preserve the final original ErrorRecord and never establish complete cleanup.
- **Compute Image nested-operation polling:** recognize only a structured subscription-deployment GET/404/DeploymentNotFound for a different nested deployment, with matching subscription, ARM endpoint, request path, typed body and raw response. Observe the exact original root ID using scoped status reads and the captured context. Only authoritative Succeeded returns its actual outputs. Confirmed Failed retains the original error and goes through existing classification and complete cleanup; ongoing, unknown, malformed or unreadable outcomes cannot authorize another submission. This path never uses legacy automatic replay.
- **Safety controls:** distinguish canceled HttpClient deadline tokens from caller cancellation; inspect independent RuntimeException error branches; reject malformed HTTP status and mixed successful/error operation envelopes. Preserve permission and cancellation priority, paginated/Graph-aware discovery, three region candidates and three actual submissions, deployment-script and same-region restrictions, pinned/global/fixed-secondary behavior, and full resource plus deployment-history cleanup. No DELETE, deployment submission, or template-export POST is newly retried.

The [function-optimized Container App failure](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/actions/runs/37785195552/job/113341125402) is a negative control: after a successful init, a genuine terminal DeploymentFailed containing Microsoft.App/containerApps ResourceNotFound remains a failure, not polling recovery success or an extra submission. No module repair is included.

### Bounded file scope

## Description

<!--

Repairs two generic environment-setup failures independently of AVM module changes:

- [Missing PSGallery after default registration](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/actions/runs/37830691300/job/113495136928).
- [Invalid powershell-yaml 0.4.2 archive](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/actions/runs/37830691300/job/113495138664).

`Install-CustomModule` still reuses installed matching modules before any repository access. It now confirms that default registration actually created PSGallery and permits one additional registration attempt only when the command returned normally but the repository is still absent. Explicit repository errors remain terminal.

Archive recovery is deliberately narrow: one additional installation of the same resolved object, only for the exact NuGet `InvalidResult` error identifying the requested package and missing ZIP end-of-central-directory record, with explicitly empty dependency metadata. It requires loaded PowerShellGet 2.2.5, PackageManagement 1.4.8.1, and the NuGet provider reporting 3.0.0.1 (its inspected assembly version is 3.0.0.2). Other runtimes, dependencies, errors, or a second failure terminate normally. These are recovery guards, not package-version upgrades or global configuration changes.

Successful installation must resolve the exact version and import its exact manifest, checking the returned name, version, and module directory. The old module-unloading block is removed; an incompatible loaded module is not replaced. `ShouldProcess` and existing installation flags are preserved. No shared caches are deleted and no TLS, signature, or publisher controls are newly disabled.

### Recovery evidence and limits

The installed PowerShellGet 2.2.5 implementation can suppress failed endpoint resolution inside `Set-PSGalleryRepository` and return without creating a repository. Its `Install-PackageUtility` creates an operation-specific staging directory before provider installation and promotes modules only after extraction and manifest validation. The inspected source SHA-256 is `573D4A3861CB967E52EAF6155A41F930FCD4168368A6946F65D985F30DC357EC`.

An offline probe exercised the installed NuGet assembly with an injected HTTP handler: the first response reproduced the exact wrapped archive error and yielded no package or extracted module files; the second issued another HTTP request and produced a usable synthetic module. Existing sentinel state remained unchanged. The same failure fields, forwarded according to the inspected PackageManagement error-record contract, exercised the production bootstrap against the real loaded runtime versions and recovered in exactly two attempts.

Relevant immutable provider source: [download, extraction, and error handling](https://github.com/OneGet/NuGetProvider/blob/6c486d0de4f4c550615467d2b1298e5fb0cdcd2b/NugetLightClient.cs), [ZIP extraction](https://github.com/OneGet/NuGetProvider/blob/6c486d0de4f4c550615467d2b1298e5fb0cdcd2b/Utility/PackageUtility.cs), and [provider error forwarding](https://github.com/OneGet/NuGetProvider/blob/6c486d0de4f4c550615467d2b1298e5fb0cdcd2b/Sdk/Request.cs). Requiring no declared dependencies avoids replaying installations after earlier dependencies might have been processed. A new PowerShellGet invocation obtains fresh staging; recovery does not depend on deleting a shared cache.

The probe ran on Windows PowerShell Core 7.6.6 with synthetic packages, not the historical Linux runner. The original bad response and exact historical provider versions were not captured, so this does not attribute the failure to truncation, a proxy, or a corrupt cache. Unknown runtime/error contracts are intentionally not retried.

Only the shared bootstrap script and its tests change. No module files, workflow definitions, dependency versions, or commits from other open branches are included.

Prevent an unusable latest-Bicep download from replacing the working compiler during agent setup.

- Download the same official latest Linux x64 release into a unique temporary file, with HTTP failure detection.
- Check native exit codes and retain diagnostics for download, executable permissions, candidate validation, promotion, and the installed version check.
- Require the candidate to run `--version` successfully and report a Bicep version before replacing `/usr/local/bin/bicep`.
- Clean up the candidate on failure without hiding the original error. Stop setup rather than silently using the older compiler.
- Keep error preferences local to the installer helper; PowerShell dependency installation and unrelated environment setup are unchanged.

There are no new dependencies, version pins, retries, sleeps, or TLS/signature bypasses. All new regression tests use offline command mocks and isolated Pester fixture files.

**Immutable failure evidence:** [run 37855248179, job 113579539000](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/actions/runs/37855248179/job/113579539000), at commit `9dbf38e8b2ea2278f9feb93a35ed139806b42f59`. prs.author: Theuno
prs.body:
## Description

Fixes a bug in `avm/res/event-hub/namespace` where setting `captureDescription.enabled: false` caused the **entire** `captureDescription` block to be silently dropped from the deployed event hub, instead of being deployed with capture turned off.

The child module guarded emission of the block on `enabled != false`:

```diff
-...(!empty(captureDescription) && (captureDescription!.?enabled != false)
+...(!empty(captureDescription)
   ? {
       captureDescription: {
-        destination: {
-          name: captureDescription!.destination!.?name
-          identity: captureIdentity
-          properties: captureDescription!.destination!.?properties
-        }
+        ...(!empty(captureDescription!.?destination)
+          ? {
+              destination: {
+                name: captureDescription!.destination!.?name
+                identity: captureIdentity
+                properties: captureDescription!.destination!.?properties
+              }
+            }
+          : {})
         enabled: captureDescription!.?enabled ?? true
```

Consequences of the old behaviour:

- `destination`, `encoding`, `intervalInSeconds`, `sizeLimitInBytes` and `skipEmptyArchives` were all lost whenever capture was disabled.
- Deployed state diverged from declared configuration — the template described a capture config that did not exist on the resource.
- Re-enabling capture later required re-supplying every setting, rather than flipping a single boolean.

With this change the block is emitted whenever it is provided, `enabled` still defaults to `true` when omitted, and `destination` is now emitted conditionally so a destination-less configuration no longer produces an incomplete object.

No public issue exists for this bug; it was found and reproduced while consuming the published module.

## Pipeline Reference

| Pipeline |
| -------- |
| [![avm.res.event-hub.namespace](https://github.com/Theuno/bicep-registry-modules/actions/workflows/avm.res.event-hub.namespace.yml/badge.svg?branch=users%2FTheuno%2Favm-res-event-hub-namespace-capture-enabled-false)](https://github.com/Theuno/bicep-registry-modules/actions/runs/37850017211) |

## Type of Change

- Azure Verified Module updates:
  - [x] Bugfix containing backwards-compatible bug fixes, and I have NOT bumped the MAJOR or MINOR version in `version.json`:
  - [ ] Feature update backwards compatible feature updates, and I have bumped the MINOR version in `version.json`.
  - [ ] Breaking changes and I have bumped the MAJOR version in `version.json`.
  - [ ] Update to documentation
- [ ] Update to CI Environment or utilities (Non-module affecting changes)

## Checklist

- [x] I'm sure there are no other open Pull Requests for the same update/change
- [x] I have run `Set-AVMModule` locally to generate the supporting module files.
- [x] My corresponding pipelines / checks run clean and green without any errors or warnings
- [x] I have updated the module's CHANGELOG.md file with an entry for the next version

---

## Evidence

Both the published module and this branch were deployed to a live subscription with identical input:

```bicep
captureDescription: {
  enabled: false
  destination: { name: 'EventHubArchive.AzureBlockBlob', properties: { ... } }
  encoding: 'Avro'
  intervalInSeconds: 300
}
```

**Before** — `br/public:avm/res/event-hub/namespace:0.15.1`:

```console
$ az eventhubs eventhub show ... --query captureDescription
null
```

**After** — this branch:

```console
$ az eventhubs eventhub show ... --query captureDescription
{
  "enabled": false,
  "encoding": "Avro",
  "intervalInSeconds": 300,
  "destination": { "name": "EventHubArchive.AzureBlockBlob", ... }
}
```

Regression coverage was added to the `max` e2e test — event hub `-004` with `captureDescription.enabled: false` plus a full destination (user-assigned identity + storage account). That test deploys green in the pipeline run linked above, which also exercises the managed-identity capture path.

Behaviour matrix, verified live:

| Input | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `enabled: false` + destination | `enabled: false`, destination retained |
| `enabled` omitted | `enabled: true` (unchanged default) |
| `captureDescription` omitted | `null` (unchanged) |

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way — revert is a single-commit rollback of a patch version.

**Blast Radius:** narrow.

Only consumers that pass `captureDescription` are affected, and only the `enabled: false` case changes outcome. Previously that input produced no capture configuration at all; it now produces a disabled capture configuration — which is what the template asked for. Callers omitting `captureDescription`, or passing it with `enabled` true/omitted, see byte-identical output.

One behavioural note for existing consumers: a deployment that currently relies on `enabled: false` as a way to *remove* capture settings will now retain them on the resource. Capture remains off either way, so there is no data-plane impact.

Follow-up to merged [#7492](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/pull/7492), containing the preserved authorization-replay repair and one bounded CI setup correction. No module, workflow, dependency, permission, or deployment-policy changes are included.

**Setup rejection:** the [failed setup job](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/actions/runs/37919966028/job/113785385892) successfully validates Bicep 0.48.1, then rejects the imported `powershell-yaml` 0.4.2 module. An offline reproduction using the already-installed actual package shows that `Import-Module -PassThru` returns `Load-Assemblies` 0.0 metadata from `ScriptsToProcess`, followed by the correct, usable `powershell-yaml` 0.4.2 module. Select the exact requested name from that output, then retain the single-match, exact-version, and platform-aware origin checks. Compiler safeguards, bounded archive retry, initialization errors, WhatIf, and caller error preferences remain intact. The real package passes the repaired helper with catalog and installation calls stubbed; both YAML conversion commands remain usable.

**Authorization replay:** structured authorization denials veto legacy retry on both returned-result and observed thrown-failure paths. Returned Failed results require the exact scoped Failed root and complete structured operation errors; failed reads preserve the original error records and stop. Existing positive quota/legacy retries, three-region/three-submission limits, retention, cleanup-before-relocation, cancellation priority, and no replay of Running/unknown roots remain unchanged. The four existing failed-but-created fixtures supply the newly required Failed-state and structured error evidence without weakening their original assertions.

| # | File | Change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `utilities\pipelines\sharedScripts\Set-EnvironmentOnAgent.ps1` | Validate the unique exact-name requested module separately from initializer metadata. |
| 2 | `utilities\tests\pipelines\Set-EnvironmentOnAgent.Tests.ps1` | Add actual-manifest and import-identity regression coverage, including conflicting imports and initialization failures. |
| 3 | `utilities\pipelines\e2eValidation\resourceDeployment\Invoke-TemplateDeploymentWithRetry.ps1` | Veto structured authorization denials before coordinated legacy retry. |
| 4 | `utilities\pipelines\e2eValidation\resourceDeployment\New-TemplateDeployment.ps1` | Classify structured denials and require trustworthy returned-failure evidence before replay. |
| 5 | `utilities\tests\pipelines\DeploymentCleanupWorkflow.Tests.ps1` | Cover direct callers, failed reads, and authorization failures while preserving cleanup assertions. |
| 6 | `utilities\tests\pipelines\Invoke-TemplateDeploymentWithRetry.Tests.ps1` | Cover authorization replay prevention and retained positive retry controls. |

### Offline validation

Final committed head: `14a9cca3b24ec0580a1601b140deb93f92daff07`; tree: `c8dec57b1b8da7e3771da1c4d5cdb2b416ce6d71`. The unchanged authorization commit `9995513260c705198c683843e2113c88b22eda45` precedes the two-file setup commit, on accepted main `bbe2e90b3d40b8d2a362c2b80782a7e8ad1e6fbd`.

Executed with the preserved offline runner (SHA256 `D495830F278F634A685040494DDD8AB57802E7EDD3BF37736CCDED64A3839B5B`), configured Pester initialized before containers, isolated short TEMP/TMP/TMPDIR plus AVM_HOME/module-analysis cache, and `AVM_NO_AUTO_INSTALL=1`. Only installed tools were used.

```powershell
$evidence = Join-Path $HOME '.copilot\session-state\bf478d9d-1dc5-4be7-9795-231bb28907b2\files'
. (Join-Path $evidence 'Invoke-ReadRecoveryTests.ps1')

Invoke-ReadRecoveryTests -Label 'yaml-import-setup-red-v2' -TestFiles @('Set-EnvironmentOnAgent.Tests.ps1') -BaselineRef '9995513260c705198c683843e2113c88b22eda45'
Invoke-ReadRecoveryTests -Label 'yaml-import-setup-green-v2' -TestFiles @('Set-EnvironmentOnAgent.Tests.ps1')

Invoke-ReadRecoveryTests -Label 'authorization-setup-final-eight-suites' -TestFiles @(
    'DeploymentResponseContracts.Tests.ps1',
    'Invoke-TemplateDeploymentWithRetry.Tests.ps1',
    'Test-TemplateDeploymentWithRetry.Tests.ps1',
    'RegionalPreflightValidation.Tests.ps1',
    'RegionalValidationWorkflow.Tests.ps1',
    'DeploymentCleanupWorkflow.Tests.ps1',
    'ServiceRegionalRetry.Tests.ps1',
    'Set-EnvironmentOnAgent.Tests.ps1'
)

git diff --check bbe2e90b3d40b8d2a362c2b80782a7e8ad1e6fbd HEAD
```

Results: setup red **6 failed / 69 passed**, each failure reproducing the import rejection; setup green **75 passed / 0 failed** with identical test bytes. The final committed eight-suite run passed **1,715 / 0 failed / 0 skipped / 0 unselected**, with **572 expected warnings**. Its exact case identities and multiplicities match the preserved 1,640 deployment cases plus all 75 setup cases. These include 66 authorization cases and 15 new setup cases. Whitespace validation passed.

PowerShell parser checks found zero errors. PSScriptAnalyzer 1.25.0 comparisons invoked `Invoke-ScriptAnalyzer -ScriptDefinition $baselineText` and `Invoke-ScriptAnalyzer -ScriptDefinition $currentText` for all six files, stripping UTF-8 BOMs symmetrically from the accepted-main/current Git text: **zero added rule/message/multiplicity findings**. `Install-BicepCli` and the `Set-EnvironmentOnAgent` orchestration function are text-identical to accepted main. Raw receipts and hashes are preserved outside the repository.

**Limitations:** these are offline checks, not evidence of historical live recovery. The setup logs do not expose the returned import records; that contract was reproduced with the actual installed 0.4.2 package on Windows PowerShell 7.6.6, not the historical Linux runner. The authorization denial wording and returned-versus-thrown sequence came from [this historical job](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/actions/runs/37898417439/job/113720010492), but historical SDK exception types/categories and complete ARM responses were not captured. Closes #123

Adds an export-only Bicep naming utility at the **proposed** path `avm/utl/general/naming`, initially version `0.1.0`. Development was explicitly authorized before formal proposal approval. Related proposal [Azure/Azure-Verified-Modules#3059](https://github.com/Azure/Azure-Verified-Modules/issues/3059) remains open; this draft does not claim program approval.

The modern [Terraform AVM naming utility](https://github.com/Azure/terraform-azure-avm-utl-naming/tree/f74c017ea99d76f4109a78d99eea79dcac335240) is authoritative, pinned to `f74c017ea99d76f4109a78d99eea79dcac335240`. Its two catalogs, two schemas and license are copied byte-for-byte. Generated JSON chunks preserve every resource and envelope property without altering those snapshots. `.gitattributes` prevents Git line-ending conversion of upstream files.

**API and behavior**

- Exports `getName`, `getNames`, `getNamesByResourceType`, `getCatalog`, the merged catalog and input types. Naming requires no nested deployment, deployment script, cloud compute or runtime Terraform invocation.
- Supports compact prefixes/suffixes, catalog slugs and overrides, casing, bounds, numbered instances, supported templates, fixed names, UUID names, token-retention diagnostics and optional strict validation. Catalog merging replaces whole properties rather than recursively merging metadata or arrays.
- `uniqueSeed` is an exact Terraform-compatible token source. Alternatively, `uniqueIdentity`, `uniqueScope` and `uniqueAttempt` derive deterministic Bicep tokens from the full, untruncated identity. Reusing inputs and a pinned module version reproduces names; changing caller-owned identity allows fresh names. The utility creates no random or persisted state.
- The downstream workflow reads immutable Terraform files, regenerates and checks artifacts, and proposes a new draft. It protects existing update branches/reviews, never executes downloaded code, and does not scrape Azure rules, merge, deploy or publish.

**Explicit compatibility boundaries**

Common explicit-seed ASCII inputs match the Terraform implementation. Bicep-derived identities are a new mode, not Terraform random seeds. Terraform's persisted randomness, frozen legacy renderer and arbitrary HCL template expressions are not ported. Native `guid` uses a different namespace from Terraform's URL UUID namespace, so UUID values intentionally differ. Custom template-token names cannot collide with built-ins even by case. Unicode length/casing use ARM semantics.

Validation never reports success for missing constraints or unsupported regexes. The 48 supported descriptors include distinct `^Default$` and `^default$` records. At this source revision, **336 of 579 entries** have complete native validation, versus **337 in Terraform**: `policy_definition` uses a Unicode control-category pattern outside the supported native subset. Its validation is explicitly incomplete and `requireValidNames` rejects it. `nameAvailable` means a candidate was rendered, not that Azure accepts it or that the name is unused.

|---|------|--------|
| 1 | `avm/utl/general/naming/main.bicep`, `main.json` | Pure naming API, typed inputs, deterministic identities, rendering, diagnostics and compiled exports. |

| 8 | `utilities/pipelines/staticValidation/compliance/module.tests.ps1`; `utilities/tests/pipelines/NamingCatalog.Tests.ps1` | Recognizes compiler-qualified import variables without relaxing authored-name checks; adds catalog, descriptor, workflow and documentation regressions. |

Separate the shared HCI image builder's build region from the persistent resource locations, while preserving existing names, version `26.1.0`, defaults, and output contracts.

| PowerShell input | Bicep input | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `BuildLocation` | `buildLocation` | `Location` / `location` |
| `ReplicationRegions` (`string[]`) | `replicationRegions` (`string[]`) | `[Location]` / `[location]` |

`Location` still controls the resource group, gallery, image definition, managed identity, and subscription-deployment location. Only the image template/build VM uses `BuildLocation`. Effective replication regions are the deduplicated union of the image-definition location, build location, and requested regions, using the supported AIB `targetRegions` field with one Standard_LRS replica per region.

AIB creates the gallery image version in the image definition's location, even when the build is elsewhere, and the version's source region must be a replication target. An existing template at a different build location is rejected with instructions to select a new `ImageTemplateName`; no resources are deleted or moved.

All gallery-version reads request `$expand=ReplicationStatus`. Skip, resume, and publication-wait paths require every required region to be configured and report `Completed`. An existing unavailable version fails without deploying or starting another build. New/resumed builds fail on terminal publication/replication problems and use the existing timeout budget for in-progress or missing replication status. The helper's comment-based help documents the contract.

Official references:
- [AIB gallery distribution and image-version location](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/linux/image-builder-json#distribute-sharedimage)
- [Compute Gallery source-region requirement](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/shared-image-galleries#frequently-asked-questions)
- [Gallery image-version replication status](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/compute/gallery-image-versions/get)

## Description

<!--
>Thank you for your contribution !
> Please include a summary of the change and which issue is fixed.
> Please also include the context.
> List any dependencies that are required for this change.

No linked issue; the demonstrated defaults deployment incident is referenced below.
-->

Fix the shared-CI status-recovery window mismatch demonstrated by the [Log Analytics defaults deployment](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/actions/runs/38088010240/job/114318808902). A genuine 100-second HttpClient timeout entered recovery, which observed the same Running root until its one-hour window expired. Microsoft documents that [dedicated cluster creation typically takes two hours and asynchronous operations can take a few hours](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/logs/logs-dedicated-clusters).

The deployment coordinator now computes one absolute UTC recovery deadline four hours after entry and passes it through both deployment helpers to all three existing recovery paths: typed submission timeouts, nested operation-read reconciliation, and management-group HTTP 403 reconciliation. Attempts, validation time, and subsequent request errors do not reset it. Direct callers without the optional deadline retain their one-hour default. Invalid/non-UTC deadlines are rejected, status reads completing at or after expiration fail closed, and fractional final polling delays are preserved instead of being rounded to zero.

This fixes observation after the demonstrated defaults client timeout, **not a provider stall or native provisioning timeout**. The separate Log Analytics WAF deployment polled natively for roughly four hours before returning ResourceDeploymentFailure; it never entered this one-hour recovery-expiry path and is not repaired by this change. Existing identity checks, cancellation/authentication handling, three consecutive typed-read-timeout limit, attempt/region budgets, retained-resource behavior, and cleanup tracking remain in place. No forced cleanup, module changes, hosted timeout increase, login-condition changes, or other repairs are included. No new dependencies.

**Preparation and regression coverage only; not a caller migration or rollout.**

This draft contains two source-only commits, `926dff86f4f36c4b8529990e37cb3a044465bd96` and `609c53ccab80878a21dddd294165ca2b171446b3`, based on registry main `2ab9cb3b6728393f07fe85ab6267e162f3b7a93c`.

- Explicitly check out `github.sha` before the generic workflow resolves modules, retaining merge-commit validation for pull requests.
- Cover ordinary caller filenames and canonical roots, child/bulk root selection, unchanged generic deployment controls, and rejection of caller-level identity overrides.
- Add `.avm/child-module-publish-allowed-list.json` with exactly the existing approvals. Keep the legacy configuration unchanged and enforce case-sensitive JSON parity.
- Preserve coordinated manual tools upgrades with the two approved narrow Dependabot ignores; other action updates remain enabled.
- Document the intended module-identity interface, immutable tools pins, package/federation prerequisites, and limits on retiring current registry helpers and tests.

Generic deployment remains supported. The intended tools route will select identities from the validated flat `VALIDATE_MODULE_CLIENT_IDS` mapping without a new caller identity input or an old shared-client fallback. This selection is a workflow-code convention, **not a per-module federation security boundary**.

All actual callers still reference the existing local reusable workflows. There is no placeholder or unpublished tools pin in these commits. The prepared remote-reference rewrites and their two pending test suites are excluded from this draft. No shared template, action, helper or existing regression suite is removed.

Remote-reference migration remains blocked on a qualified published executable tools revision, a compatible package, and the matching federation source/rollout approval. ## Description

<!--
>Thank you for your contribution !

Closes #123
-->

Adds the optional repository-root `.required-resource-providers.json`, using the same exact-module-path-to-string-array format as `.required-features.json`, with provider namespaces instead of feature names. The existing feature manifest is unchanged. The initial consumer is `avm/res/hybrid-container-service/provisioned-cluster-instance`, with the 13 prerequisites documented in [Azure Local deployment permissions](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-local/deploy/deployment-arc-register-server-permissions?view=azloc-2609).

The deployment action registers providers immediately after feature registration and before token replacement, validation, or deployment, using the selected test subscription and login tenant. Registered providers are skipped, existing Registering operations are awaited without resubmission, and NotRegistered/Unregistered providers are registered once and awaited. Invalid declarations, identity mismatches, approval-required/unknown states, command errors, and timeouts fail explicitly. Missing, empty, or unrelated declarations are logged no-ops without Azure calls; WhatIf also avoids Azure calls. The entire provider map is validated before registration begins.

The implementation reuses the existing feature helper's validated parser, account checks, native argument handling, 60-second command timeout, and bounded state polling. Existing feature registration and provider-refresh behavior are retained. No new dependency, Azure account switching, permission grants, consent flags, unregister cleanup, Bicep changes, HCI host-script changes, or image-builder changes are introduced. The deployment identity needs the declared providers' subscription-scoped `/register/action` permissions.

The coupled feature-workflow suite had one failing baseline assertion against the already-existing failure-cleanup login condition. This change corrects that assertion without changing cleanup behavior. Comment-based help and the action input description document both prerequisite files.

```powershell

$sourcePaths = @(
  '.\utilities\pipelines\sharedScripts\Register-RequiredSubscriptionFeature.ps1',

  $tokens = $null; $parseErrors = $null
  $null = [System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile((Join-Path $PWD.Path $path), [ref] $tokens, [ref] $parseErrors)
  if ($parseErrors.Count) { throw ($parseErrors | Out-String) }
  $bytes = [System.IO.File]::ReadAllBytes((Join-Path $PWD.Path $path))
  if ($bytes[0] -ne 0xEF -or $bytes[1] -ne 0xBB -or $bytes[2] -ne 0xBF) { throw "Missing UTF-8 BOM: $path" }
  if ($bytes[-1] -ne 10 -or $bytes -contains 13) { throw "Unexpected line endings: $path" }
}
$diagnostics = @(
  foreach ($path in $sourcePaths) { Invoke-ScriptAnalyzer -Path $path -Severity Error,Warning }
  foreach ($path in $testPaths) { Invoke-ScriptAnalyzer -Path $path -Severity Error,Warning -ExcludeRule PSReviewUnusedParameter,PSUseDeclaredVarsMoreThanAssignments }

$action = ConvertFrom-Yaml -Yaml (Get-Content -LiteralPath '.\.github\actions\templates\avm-validateModuleDeployment\action.yml' -Raw)
foreach ($id in @('register-required-features', 'register-required-resource-providers')) {

  $null = [System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseInput($step[0].run, [ref] $tokens, [ref] $parseErrors)
  if ($parseErrors.Count) { throw ($parseErrors | Out-String) }
}
$manifest = Get-Content -LiteralPath '.\.required-resource-providers.json' -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json -AsHashtable
if ($manifest.Count -ne 1 -or $manifest['avm/res/hybrid-container-service/provisioned-cluster-instance'].Count -ne 13) { throw 'Unexpected provider declaration scope.' }
Write-Output 'PASS: 5 PowerShell files, UTF-8 BOM/LF formatting, applicable analyzer rules, action YAML and both inline scripts, HCI-only 13-provider manifest.'

```

## Description

Closes #123

**Draft source-only policy proposal for review. This is not approval to activate, merge or run another HCI deployment. The overall HCI campaign remains incomplete.**

The [historical HCI run](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/actions/runs/38180488157) correctly observed the original deployment after a submission timeout, but defaults reached the existing four-hour recovery deadline while that root was still running. This proposal changes only generic CI source; it does not change HCI fixtures, Kubernetes readiness, retry classification, the three-region/three-attempt limits, or the separate work in [#7483](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/pull/7483).

For the exact module `avm/res/hybrid-container-service/provisioned-cluster-instance`, the deployment action supplies the verified current GitHub-hosted job start. Recovery then uses one immutable UTC deadline:

`min(coordinator entry + 315 minutes, actual job start + 320 minutes)`

The job-age cap includes setup/prerequisites and is not renewed for later coordinator/idempotency calls. Other modules keep four hours and make no new metadata requests. Standalone coordinator callers remain at four hours without the optional job timing; standalone deployment/status-wait callers retain their existing defaults, including the one-hour wait.

Job identity uses the now-documented [`job.check_run_id`](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/contexts#job-context), matched against every page of the exact [workflow run-attempt jobs endpoint](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/actions/workflow-jobs#list-jobs-for-a-workflow-run-attempt). The selected job must also match run ID, attempt, event-specific head SHA, runner and active state. `pull_request` uses `github.event.pull_request.head.sha`, not the synthetic merge SHA in `github.sha`; push/dispatch use `github.sha`. Timestamps require an explicit offset and are normalized to UTC.

Metadata reads are anonymous and GitHub.com-only: no tokens, credential fallback, redirects, arbitrary pagination links or added GitHub/Azure permissions. Pagination is bounded to 20 pages of 100 jobs, with connection/operation timeouts and no HTTP retries. Missing, ambiguous, inconsistent, invalid, future or exhausted metadata, anonymous rate limits, API failures and inaccessible/private repositories fail before resource deployment; there is no fresh-window fallback.

Before any bounded submission, the remaining allowance is checked again, including after validation and slow context preparation. Expiration does not fabricate a deployment owner or authorize another POST. An already submitted root retains its original name and cleanup ownership. Opt-in bounded resource-group submissions require an existing resource group rather than creating an untracked group before the deadline check. Ordinary resource-group creation is unchanged.

**Policy assumptions and unresolved runtime limit:** GitHub-hosted jobs have a [six-hour hard limit](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits), and the current reusable deployment workflow has no shorter custom timeout. The earlier 320-minute cap targets at least 30 minutes for cleanup plus 10 minutes of in-flight request/return headroom. This is a recovery-policy reserve, **not a hard whole-job guarantee**: a blocking native Azure submission/status call or cleanup can exceed it. Those calls are not interrupted, no job/step timeout is added, and the existing post-coordinator output/cleanup ownership protocol is not replaced. Actual runner metadata availability, anonymous quota and live HCI behavior remain unverified. Integration/activation requires a separate review decision.

No new packages, workflow permissions, provider registrations, image/BAMI operations, Azure/Graph calls, E2E labels, workflow dispatches or merges were performed for this proposal. The internal runbook needs a corresponding follow-up in [azure-cloud-native/Azure-Verified-Modules-Docs#52](https://msft.ghe.com/azure-cloud-native/Azure-Verified-Modules-Docs/pull/52); that document is outside this change.

| Live Azure/E2E execution: **not run**. No workflow was dispatched and no E2E labels were added. |

Exact reproducible focused proof command, run against commit `14403febb7d3524dd0c4b987782eeb3bb8423562` (PowerShell 7.6.6, Pester 5.7.1, Avm.Authoring 0.22.1): **passed, 174/174**. The expected offline Gallery-version-check warning is emitted by initialization; dependencies were not installed.

## Description

Adds an optional `identitySettings` parameter to `avm/res/app/job` and passes it through to `properties.configuration.identitySettings`. Adds support for creating user-defined runtime environments in an Azure Automation Account and selecting those environments when defining runbooks.

Changes include:

- Extended the max example with PowerShell 7.4 and Python 3.10 environments, with `TestRunbook` referencing the PowerShell environment.
- Regenerated ARM templates and README documentation using `Set-AVMModule`.
- Updated the parent and runbook changelogs.

The runtime-environment module is internal and is not independently published. Custom package installation through the runtime-environment `packages` child resource is outside this change's scope.

## Description

<!--
