Fixes #123
Closes #123
-->

Correct the dedicated HCI setup's provider-registration guard. `Get-AzResourceProvider -ProviderNamespace` emits a separate record for each resource type, so requiring exactly one record rejects a registered provider. This blocked the Begin job in [setup run 38452972955](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/actions/runs/38452972955).

The guard now requires a nonempty collection in which **every** record has the exact requested namespace and `Registered` state. Empty, null, incomplete, wrong-namespace, wrong-case, unregistered and mixed responses still stop before preparation.

Add twelve regressions through the real `Invoke-HciPreparationStep -Stage Begin` entry point, using existing offline Azure mocks. Successful cases cover one and multiple resource-type records; rejected cases assert no preparation resource reads or writes. Pin the shared Azure Local 2601 host-image payload to the supplied public mirror and require SHA256 verification of the downloaded VHDX before the Image Builder customizer can succeed.

- Source: https://jumpstartprodsg.blob.core.windows.net/jslocal/localbox/prod/AzLocal2601.vhdx
- Published checksum: https://jumpstartprodsg.blob.core.windows.net/jslocal/localbox/prod/AzLocal2601.sha256
- Pinned SHA256: `3a797826d7e7ae7abc55d1071322ddecc80575c2356fea9e74818ab9f6720a1f`

The previous build failed when its old source rejected anonymous access with `PublicAccessNotPermitted`. On 2026-10-14 at 14:45 UTC, a certificate-validating metadata-only request to the supplied mirror returned HTTP 200 (12,719,226,880 bytes), and a bounded checksum request returned the complete 64-byte SHA256 file. No VHDX bytes were downloaded locally; the build must still verify the actual payload.

`environment.json` now declares the source and digest. The subscription template loads those shared defaults, and the preparation helper explicitly forwards both values through the existing builder. The customizer checks digest format, preserves bounded download retries, hashes the resulting file, and fails on missing, partial, empty, mismatched or unreadable data. Generic callers overriding the source must supply its matching digest.

This intentionally changes the full `avm-contract` from `a9c4a7460731465d7e2b2ca5ab5072c20585574ab558de164da41e360820ebf1` to `c9b8ed2ccc700a6280b7200a74b227a91b3f86a38cac6a21d5908b58dcba62cf`. Existing groups with the old contract remain blocked; this change does not adopt or migrate them automatically. Tests cover all four group guards and both configuration fields.

Australia East, image version 26.1.0, VM sizes, identities, ownership checks, deadlines, `recreate=false`, and the native-header safeguards from [#7532](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/pull/7532) remain unchanged. No workflow, BAMI caching, storage account, access grant or recovery framework is added.

**Runtime remains held.** No Azure tag/resource changes, template deletion, full payload transfer, foundation action or replacement build was performed. Future recovery needs separately checked fresh terminal/no-output/ownership evidence, a complete inventory of the provider's staging-resource deletion cascade, verified deletion settlement, and an explicit four-group contract/new-generation transition. The previous control-only reset is not sufficient. Existing Image Builder templates cannot be updated in place; deleting the exact failed template also affects its provider-created staging resources, not merely the template ARM record. The preserved failure evidence must precede any such action. Galleries, image definitions, identities and all four groups must be retained.

NOTE: This is a temporary solution until we move to the new tool chain the next week or so. We'll clean up a lot of this stuff then.

Fixes the workflow-expansion regression in [Data Factory run 38599813573](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/actions/runs/38599813573). The shared deployment workflow introduced by [#7525](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/pull/7525) evaluated `job_hci_environment` concurrency from an empty `environmentConcurrencyGroup` for ordinary tests. GitHub rejected the reusable workflow before the normal deployment jobs could start; the conditional job guard did not prevent that evaluation.

Remove the HCI job, its generic-job gate, and its matrix lock fields from the ordinary deployment path. One dedicated `avm.template.hci.module.yml` wrapper now serves the seven existing reserved module entrypoints and reuses the guarded HCI consumer. Only that wrapper adds the canonical environment lock, and the consumer retains both the cross-module environment lock and the original module/subscription lock.

The neutral deployment-selection guard defaults to `General`; the dedicated wrapper explicitly accepts `Azure Local`. An active reserved deployment through a generic manual or experimental caller now fails before login with a dedicated-workflow message. It does not fall back to a General subscription, silently omit a case, or bypass ownership checks. Generic static/PSRule-only requests and deliberately ignored reporting remain allowed. The maintenance inventory helper, generic deployment action, ordinary module/preview/manual-publish templates, explicit publish-only path, Data Factory templates, cleanup logic, and HCI preparation source are unchanged.

The HCI wrapper preserves the existing separate static, required PSRule, and optional PSRule actions and conditions. Optional PSRule does not become a deployment dependency. Publishing still requires both static and deployment success on canonical main. Regressions inspect actual downstream output contracts and reject missing-output shortcuts to publishing; no replacement output or dispatch framework is introduced.

This is a source-only repair. No workflow rerun, Azure deployment, HCI recovery deletion, contract/tag migration, new image build, configuration-secret read, or operational inventory was performed. HCI recovery remains on hold.

Keep the complete Image Builder operation URI in a dedicated, private Block Blob receipt instead of truncating or exposing a signed operation URL in resource tags.

## Description

<!--
>Thank you for your contribution !

No linked issue.
-->

Add optional, strongly typed `galleryApplications` support to `avm/res/compute/virtual-machine-scale-set`.

Contribution commit: `3dde86e4b1a6575bc33e171c97937c7cba6818be`. Its VMSS contents are the same contents used for the local and real Azure verification below. The contribution contains only the nine VMSS implementation, generated documentation, release metadata, and test files; no Copilot instruction or fork-configuration changes are included.

The parameter assigns existing Compute Gallery Application Versions to
`properties.virtualMachineProfile.applicationProfile.galleryApplications` in the common scale set model. It supports Flexible and Uniform orchestration without per-instance assignment logic. The module does not create galleries, publish packages, enforce rollout, configure firewalls, or implement a compliance controller.

The exported `vmGalleryApplicationType` exposes the six Azure API fields: required `packageReferenceId`, and optional `configurationReference`, `enableAutomaticUpgrade`, `order`, `tags` (a string, not a resource-tags object), and `treatFailureAsDeploymentFailure`. The existing VMSS API version, `2024-11-01`, is unchanged.

Omitted, explicit `null`, and empty-array input all produce a null `applicationProfile`; nonempty input is passed through without dropping explicit `false` values or applying module-specific defaults. Existing VMSS configuration and defaults remain unchanged. A same-compiler comparison against the base template confirmed that only the new parameter, exported type, conditional application profile, and generated template hash changed.

Documentation explains existing-version references, whole-array ownership, per-VM installation order, failure reporting, and the distinction between updating the common model and upgrading existing instances. A new Flexible Linux fixture creates two harmless, pinned `1.0.0` application versions in isolated test dependencies; its post-deployment tests inspect the VMSS model and require marker files from both installed applications on every member VM. The fixture uses the existing SSH TCP health-probe setting and leaves the module's automatic-repair default enabled.

### Verification

Commands below run from the repository root. The Bicep binary must be on `PATH`; on this macOS environment this was set with:

```bash
export PATH="${AZURE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.azure}/bin:$PATH"
```

**Generated artifacts: completed** using PowerShell 7.6.6, Bicep 0.47.16, and Avm.Authoring 0.25.0:

```powershell
. ./utilities/tools/Set-AVMModule.ps1
Set-AVMModule -ModuleFolderPath 'avm/res/compute/virtual-machine-scale-set'
```

**Local AVM compliance and unit tests: 172 passed, 0 failed, 3 skipped** using the repository-managed Pester 5.7.1:

```powershell
. ./utilities/tools/Test-ModuleLocally.ps1
Test-ModuleLocally -TemplateFilePath 'avm/res/compute/virtual-machine-scale-set/main.bicep' -PesterTest
```

This includes 23 new tests: three contract tests and 20 consumer compilations covering omitted/null/empty/minimal/two-application input across Linux/Windows and Flexible/Uniform. The three compliance skips concern absent `privateEndpoints` and `customerManagedKey` parameters, and an existing missing `diagnosticSettings` entry in the API-version dataset.

**Bicep lint: completed with no errors**, retaining the two existing `use-recent-api-versions` warnings for the telemetry deployment and diagnostic settings. No unrelated API-version upgrades were made.

```bash
bicep lint avm/res/compute/virtual-machine-scale-set/main.bicep
bicep lint --pattern 'avm/res/compute/virtual-machine-scale-set/tests/e2e/linux.gallery-applications/*.bicep'
```

**Bicep build: passed** for the resource module and the complete Flexible Gallery Applications fixture, including its supporting resources:

```bash
bicep build avm/res/compute/virtual-machine-scale-set/main.bicep --stdout > /dev/null
bicep build avm/res/compute/virtual-machine-scale-set/tests/e2e/linux.gallery-applications/main.test.bicep --stdout > /dev/null
```

**Formatting and PowerShell syntax: passed** for the three changed Bicep files and both new PowerShell files. The scripts use the repository's UTF-8 BOM encoding.

```powershell
foreach ($file in @(
    'avm/res/compute/virtual-machine-scale-set/main.bicep'
    'avm/res/compute/virtual-machine-scale-set/tests/e2e/linux.gallery-applications/main.test.bicep'
    'avm/res/compute/virtual-machine-scale-set/tests/e2e/linux.gallery-applications/dependencies.bicep'
)) {
    $formatted = (bicep format $file --stdout | Out-String).TrimEnd()
    if ((Get-Content -LiteralPath $file -Raw).TrimEnd() -cne $formatted) {
        throw "Formatting mismatch: $file"
    }
}
foreach ($file in @(
    'avm/res/compute/virtual-machine-scale-set/tests/unit/gallery-applications.tests.ps1'
    'avm/res/compute/virtual-machine-scale-set/tests/e2e/linux.gallery-applications/tests/application-profile.tests.ps1'
)) {
    $tokens = $null
    $errors = $null
    $null = [System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile(
        (Resolve-Path $file), [ref]$tokens, [ref]$errors
    )
    if ($errors) { throw ($errors | Out-String) }
}
```

**PSRule: 12 applicable Reliability checks passed, 0 failed.** Both required baselines were invoked for the existing Linux/Windows defaults, Windows WAF-aligned, and new Gallery Applications scenarios. `CB.AVM.WAF.Security` produced no applicable rule results for the non-dependency resources; this is not claimed as positive security-test coverage. Existing dependency suppressions apply through the repository's `dep` naming convention; no rules or suppression files were changed. Input filtering was overridden only for this explicit local run so that the non-WAF feature fixture was actually evaluated.

```powershell
Import-Module PSRule -RequiredVersion 2.9.0
$options = New-PSRuleOption -Option 'utilities/pipelines/staticValidation/psrule/ps-rule.yaml' -InputPathIgnore @()
$inputs = @(
    'avm/res/compute/virtual-machine-scale-set/tests/e2e/linux.defaults/main.test.bicep'
    'avm/res/compute/virtual-machine-scale-set/tests/e2e/windows.defaults/main.test.bicep'
    'avm/res/compute/virtual-machine-scale-set/tests/e2e/windows.waf-aligned/main.test.bicep'
    'avm/res/compute/virtual-machine-scale-set/tests/e2e/linux.gallery-applications/main.test.bicep'
)
foreach ($baseline in @('Azure.Pillar.Reliability', 'CB.AVM.WAF.Security')) {
    $results = @(Invoke-PSRule -InputPath $inputs -Module PSRule.Rules.Azure `
        -Path 'utilities/pipelines/staticValidation/psrule/.ps-rule/' `
        -Baseline $baseline -Option $options -ErrorAction Stop)
    $results | Group-Object Outcome | Select-Object Name, Count
    if (@($results | Where-Object { $_.Outcome -in @('Fail', 'Error') }).Count -gt 0) {
        throw "PSRule failures in $baseline"
    }
}
```

**Whitespace check: passed.**

```bash
git diff --check
```

**Actual Azure E2E deployment and installation: passed on 2026-10-19 in `polandcentral`.** The owner confirmed that the selected subscription is newly created, empty, non-production, and dedicated to this test, and authorized all necessary Azure actions. The five required resource providers and `Microsoft.Compute/EncryptionAtHost` were registered before deployment. `Standard_D2s_v5` was available without SKU restrictions.

The final subscription deployment succeeded, including both VMSS init and idem iterations. Both post-deployment Pester tests passed: **2 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**. The first inspected the actual Flexible VMSS model and both pinned application versions with their caller settings. The second used a read-only Run Command on the single member VM to verify the exact contents of both marker files created by the Gallery Applications. No manual application installation or per-instance application assignment was used.

The first live run exposed a test-only SDK binding error: `Invoke-AzVMRunCommand -ScriptString` accepts a single string, not a string array. The post-deployment test now joins its script lines into one string and requires the success marker on its own output line. The complete live run was repeated successfully after this fix.

The temporary local harness selected the authorized context only for its process, generated unique names, and used `try/finally` cleanup. Its core deployment and test commands were:

```powershell
Disable-AzContextAutosave -Scope Process
Set-AzContext -Context $context -Scope Process
$deployment = New-AzSubscriptionDeployment -Name $deploymentName -Location 'polandcentral' `
    -TemplateFile 'avm/res/compute/virtual-machine-scale-set/tests/e2e/linux.gallery-applications/main.test.bicep' `
    -TemplateParameterObject @{
        namePrefix = $prefix
        resourceGroupName = $resourceGroupName
        location = 'polandcentral'
    } -DefaultProfile $context -ErrorAction Stop

. ./utilities/pipelines/sharedScripts/Initialize-AvmPester.ps1
Initialize-AvmPester -RepoRootPath $PWD.Path
$configuration = New-PesterConfiguration
$configuration.Run.Container = New-PesterContainer -Path (
    'avm/res/compute/virtual-machine-scale-set/tests/e2e/linux.gallery-applications/tests/application-profile.tests.ps1'
) -Data @{ TestInputData = @{ DeploymentOutputs = $deployment.Outputs } }
$configuration.Run.PassThru = $true
$configuration.Output.Verbosity = 'Detailed'
$result = Invoke-Pester -Configuration $configuration
if ($result.FailedCount -ne 0 -or $result.PassedCount -ne 2) {
    throw 'Live Gallery Applications checks failed.'
}
```

Here `$context` is the explicitly selected disposable subscription context; `$prefix`, `$resourceGroupName`, and `$deploymentName` are unique test names. The full local harness and evidence are retained with the handoff artifacts, not added as a new repository testing framework.

**Actual no-profile regression checks: 3 passed.** Three additional zero-instance Flexible scale sets were deployed using the unchanged module defaults, with the parameter omitted, explicitly null, and an empty array respectively. Each deployment succeeded; a GET using API `2024-11-01` returned capacity `0` and a null `virtualMachineProfile.applicationProfile` in all three cases. This supplements the same-compiler baseline comparison and the 20 consumer-compilation cases.

**Cleanup: verified.** Every temporary test resource group was removed, including groups from initial unsuccessful harness attempts. The subscription deployment records were removed as well. Azure automatically created `NetworkWatcher_polandcentral` in `NetworkWatcherRG` when the first test virtual network was created; its activity timestamp was confirmed to be inside the test window, and this sole automatically created resource and its empty group were also removed. The final subscription-wide inventory at `2026-10-19T13:44:15Z` contained **0 resources and 0 resource groups**. Provider and feature registrations intentionally remain enabled; Network Watcher automatic-enablement settings were not changed.

The principal cleanup commands, always scoped to the explicitly selected subscription and owned names, were:

```powershell
Remove-AzResourceGroup -Name $resourceGroupName -Force -DefaultProfile $context -ErrorAction Stop
Remove-AzSubscriptionDeployment -Name $deploymentName -DefaultProfile $context -ErrorAction Stop
Remove-AzNetworkWatcher -Name 'NetworkWatcher_polandcentral' -ResourceGroupName 'NetworkWatcherRG' `
    -Confirm:$false -DefaultProfile $context -ErrorAction Stop
Remove-AzResourceGroup -Name 'NetworkWatcherRG' -Force -DefaultProfile $context -ErrorAction Stop
@(Get-AzResource -DefaultProfile $context).Count
@(Get-AzResourceGroup -DefaultProfile $context).Count
```

The Network Watcher removal was specific to this initially empty, dedicated subscription and was guarded by checks of its identity, creation window, and absence of other resources in that group; it is not a general cleanup instruction for shared subscriptions.

GitHub CI was not dispatched, and no pipeline badge is claimed. This contribution is intended as a **draft** pending upstream review and CI.

The module version is bumped from `0.11` to `0.12`, with a `0.12.0` changelog entry and no breaking changes.

## Description

<!--

Fixes #123
Closes #123

Depends on #7472. This PR is stacked on `andyleejordan/secure-parameter-hardening` and should be retargeted to `main` after #7472 merges. It does not change that PR's credential hardening.

This is a stopgap. I've proposed Bicep linter rules in Azure/bicep#20463 (https://github.com/Azure/bicep/issues/20463) that cover the same checks in the compiler; once those ship and AVM's `bicepconfig.json` raises them to errors, this analyzer and the per-module tests can be deleted, so I'm keeping this PR as a draft for now.

The repository-wide forwarding gate needed a baseline and an exceptions file before unrelated modules could pass. That made the checker's apparent coverage broader than the analysis it actually performed. This restores the reusable analyzer without either list or the repository-wide production scan. Each of the ten hardened modules opts in through its own `tests/unit/secureParameterForwarding.tests.ps1`, following [SNFR4](https://azure.github.io/Azure-Verified-Modules/spec/SNFR4/). Modules without that test are not covered by this checker.

Each discovered secure child binding gets an independent Pester case. Active cases reject both `Mismatch` and `Unsupported`, and an empty scan fails. Seven existing gaps are visible skipped cases with reasons beside their narrow matching conditions: two APIM bindings, VM custom-script settings, two VMSS settings projections, nested managed-cluster Flux settings awaiting extension 0.3.9, and SQL secret export. Unsupported projections are pinned to the exact expression hash: this notices expression changes but does not prove the projection secure. The kubernetes-runtime module is outside this opt-in set and is unchanged.

`avm.template.module.static.yml` already calls `avm-validateModulePester/action.yml`, which discovers each module's `tests/unit` directory alongside shared compliance tests and supplies `repoRootPath` and `moduleFolderPaths` through `New-PesterContainer`. `Test-ModuleLocally` uses the same layout. Only the analyzer's synthetic and compiler-backed behavioral tests remain in platform CI.

All helper functions now have comment-based help and typed parameters. Module identity and compiler output paths are passed explicitly, exclusion lookup helpers are gone, independent cases use `-TestCases`/`-ForEach` instead of loops inside `It`, and assertions explain their expectations with `-Because`. The analyzer's help documents its bounded grammar, coverage limits, and opt-in procedure.

## Pipeline Reference

<!-- Insert your Pipeline Status Badge below -->

| Pipeline |
| -------- |
| Local CI-managed Pester 5.7.1, Bicep 0.47.16: 87 passed, 0 failed, 7 deliberately skipped |
| Installed Pester 6.2.0: behavioral suite 45 passed; module suite 42 passed and 7 deliberately skipped |
| Hosted checks are pending; no hosted result is claimed here |

```powershell

Initialize-AvmPester -RepoRootPath $PWD.Path
$paths = @("utilities/tests/pipelines/SecureParameterForwarding.Tests.ps1") + @(Get-ChildItem avm/res -Recurse -Filter secureParameterForwarding.tests.ps1 | ForEach-Object FullName)
$result = Invoke-Pester -Path $paths -Output Normal -PassThru
if ($result.FailedCount -or $result.FailedContainersCount -or $result.PassedCount -ne 87 -or $result.SkippedCount -ne 7) { exit 1 }
```

I also ran the combined suite using CI-style containers with each module's root and child `moduleFolderPaths`: **87 passed, 0 failed, 7 skipped**. Five isolated negative controls ran the actual module-local test files against mutated templates: reverting a secure cache leaf, adding a previously unseen insecure child input, changing the skipped logger sink type, changing SQL's unsupported expression, and removing all bindings. **All five failed at the intended assertion**, rather than failing discovery or being silently skipped. The compiler fixture separately verifies that removing a real `@secure()` decorator changes `Secure` to `Mismatch` after recompilation.

`git diff --check` — **passed**. ScriptAnalyzer — **passed** with all warning/error rules on the production helper; test-file lint excluded its Pester scriptblock-scope and pure in-memory `New` fixture false positives. ## Description

Both manual dispatchers expose `authoringSource` (`gallery` by default, or `repo`) and optional `authoringRef`, forwarding only those fields. A blank Gallery ref selects the latest package; a repository ref accepts a tools commit SHA, tag, or branch, with blank selecting the latest stable tag. The pinned reusable workflow handles `SkipModuleVersionCheck` internally. PR-triggered checks continue with Gallery and a blank ref. This update changes only the two immutable workflow pins; no module sources, generated artifacts, permissions, or triggers changed.

**Bounded smoke evidence:** The approved source-mode smokes ran on the earlier unmerged BRM head `1c0bb0eacbd60fb3fa6dee7bf415c0b6d2cdbb90`, pinned to tools candidate `91c442251d5aa3649ad61f1034ac2e5043567239`, not on this PR head `f0fc2b29ae575387cf0fd6a6012a25dd2eb0628b` pinned to merged tools commit `7379a19fe3ca4e97a602a6bc1d78a61be09d31e7`. The tools-tree comparison found only eight Terraform migration engine/test files differ between the candidate and merge; Bicep workflow, runtime, bootstrap, and helper files are byte-identical. The runs therefore exercise the same Bicep workflow content, but are not new lifecycle runs of this pin-only PR head.

## Description

**DO NOT MERGE. Review and preparation only.** This isolated branch temporarily replaces the registered PR-check workflow with a manual-only, read-only diagnostic probe; it is not a permanent replacement for PR checks, a cleanup fix, or resource recovery.

The probe builds Avm.Authoring from the pinned candidate [Azure/azure-verified-modules-tools#296](https://github.com/Azure/azure-verified-modules-tools/pull/296), commit `ce21d83c1ee5a4145f052f5cd53886bdb8c99fed`, and checks the historical policy-assignment identity and trusted Azure CLI and PowerShell contexts before one explicit GET invocation for the specified nested management-group deployment operations. Only fixed success text or the candidate's restricted diagnostics are emitted. Az/SDK internals may retry; one explicit invocation does not establish one physical network request.

The first user-approved run, [41138821285](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/actions/runs/41138821285), ran on head `70053f7e74a23c2240958d36a38784f6cebc3841` from 2026-10-30T22:32:41Z to 22:34:28Z. Candidate preparation, historical module-identity validation, and OIDC sign-in succeeded; the combined context guard failed before the operations GET. The underlying field or command/parser failure was suppressed. Bootstrap resolved candidate commit `ce21d83c1ee5a4145f052f5cd53886bdb8c99fed`, module version `0.0.0`, and artifact `avm-authoring-8810029c9ea04d79b414ac0a570f6827` (ID `13017766374`, SHA-256 `b9efa2a5a64db4978d31793a13ef4014e889b1628f47def1516346f4d30bfe53`).

The separately approved second run, [41140377509](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/actions/runs/41140377509), ran on head `511f5556964052196313973877042dc3c226e9ad` from 2026-10-30T22:47:08Z to 22:49:01Z. Candidate preparation, historical module-identity validation, and OIDC sign-in succeeded. Its context guard reported only `az.accountType`; all other compared fields matched, and it stopped before the operations GET. Bootstrap resolved the same candidate commit and module version `0.0.0`; artifact `avm-authoring-bd68a60e1e5c4a35a77928bd8005c6da` (ID `13017678570`) has SHA-256 `c51e6e2e0989e4331c298b227d3eadbc7b4dd687b3ac97e1574e155fe1acc171`. The guarded application client ID was `cc1ea1c9-b77a-4ab1-adf8-356240edee04`. Neither run produced a response, HTTP status, error code, or request ID; no deployment, cleanup, deletion, or recovery occurred.

The pinned [azure/login OIDC flow](https://github.com/Azure/login/blob/7184910d9eb2b1c5e48f7073824a90609bb9b6d6/src/PowerShell/AzPSScriptBuilder.ts#L86-L91) uses a federated token, and the second login step selected Az.Accounts 5.5.3. The [5.5.3 manifest](https://github.com/Azure/azure-powershell/blob/be60d361ef395f950c969c33afe54b581062eff7/src/Accounts/Accounts/Az.Accounts.psd1#L15) and [source](https://github.com/Azure/azure-powershell/blob/be60d361ef395f950c969c33afe54b581062eff7/src/Accounts/Accounts/Account/ConnectAzureRmAccount.cs#L404-L411) show that this version assigns `ClientAssertion` for that parameter set, rather than `ServicePrincipal`. The second run did not log the actual account type or the Az.Accounts version loaded in the subsequent probe process, so those values remain unproven.

The previous revision added fixed CLI availability, execution, exit, JSON, and shape categories; Az context read, cardinality, and shape categories; and allowlisted context-field mismatch names. This revision requires `ClientAssertion` for the Az account type, keeps the CLI `servicePrincipal` check and every other identity/context guard, and emits only the numeric version of the single loaded Az.Accounts module after the context read. Missing, ambiguous, or invalid version provenance fails before GET with a fixed message; raw context, account values, and errors are not emitted.

The separately approved third run, [41142635368](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/actions/runs/41142635368), succeeded on reviewed head `b8f17f4e9335638a3104f70253b0b55588c0a519` from 2026-10-30T23:08:35Z to 23:10:41Z. Bootstrap resolved repository ref/commit `ce21d83c1ee5a4145f052f5cd53886bdb8c99fed` and module version `0.0.0`; its artifact `avm-authoring-c836503829b340558bacd4b03e6ef111` (ID `13020215992`) has SHA-256 `fdad233052e867e16a7513a660cd6ced5a7029c90c9729c2a173e90e79c4cbbf`. The worker confirmed that candidate and artifact. The historical module identity, OIDC sign-in, and all CLI and Az context guards passed. The login process selected Az.Accounts `5.5.3`, while the probe process loaded `5.0.0`. One explicit operations GET returned HTTP 200 and the candidate parser accepted the response; SDK-internal retries remain possible. This is current read-access evidence for that exact endpoint only, not proof of the original failure's cause, broader effective RBAC, or cleanup correctness. No additional dispatch, Azure request, cleanup, deletion, or recovery was performed.

**Separate user approval is required before any future sign-in and GET.** Dispatch targets a branch or tag, not an immutable SHA: immediately verify that the dispatched branch still points to the newly reviewed full head SHA `b8f17f4e9335638a3104f70253b0b55588c0a519` before requesting approval and execution. This probe must never be merged or labeled for E2E.

Its strict `AllowedStatus @(200)` intentionally treats HTTP 404 as a diagnostic failure; the original cleanup reader allowed 200 and 404. The successful response is current evidence, not proof of the original failure's HTTP cause. OIDC sign-in succeeded in all three runs, but the live federation configuration and broader effective RBAC remain unverified. A login or context failure must stop before GET.

Base: `82950838e7cefc9a32e813055fbf407ea5819e15`. The prior broad qualification [#7374](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/pull/7374) remains untouched.

| [Third approved probe run](https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules/actions/runs/41142635368): succeeded; guarded operations GET returned HTTP 200. |

Module generation and changelog are not applicable: no module files changed. Broad AVM CI and E2E are intentionally not run for this one-off workflow.

- `Import-Module powershell-yaml; $w = ConvertFrom-Yaml (Get-Content -Raw '.github\workflows\pr-check.yml'); foreach ($s in $w.jobs.probe.steps) { if ($s.run) { $tokens=$null; $errors=$null; $null=[System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseInput($s.run,[ref]$tokens,[ref]$errors); if ($errors) { throw $errors[0] } } }; Write-Output 'YAML and PowerShell AST validation passed.'` — passed; YAML and both PowerShell blocks parsed.
- `$env:COPILOT_SESSION_DIR = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE '.copilot\session-state\79ae585c-8208-4004-8d4b-55f7601992e4\files'; . "$env:COPILOT_SESSION_DIR\probe-offline-tests.ps1"; Invoke-ProbeOfflineTests` — passed; `ClientAssertion` happy path, rejected `ServicePrincipal`, `User`, unknown and missing account types before GET, version provenance failures, all 12 individual context mismatches, command/shape failures, single explicit GET, sanitized output, and the read-only command boundary. This session-only harness does not contact Azure and does not prove live federation/RBAC or actual Az SDK behavior.
- `git diff --cached --check` — passed before commit.

 ## Using this template for an end-to-end HCI cluster deployment in Azure
 
-To use this Bicep module, you'll need to download a copy then supply values for the required parameters. Follow these steps:
+This walkthrough deploys a standalone cluster. Shared CI infrastructure is prepared separately by `platform.hci.prepare.yml`; ordinary CI tests validate and use the prepared environment.
 
 1. Clone the repository with Git: `git clone https://github.com/Azure/bicep-registry-modules.git`
-1. Pick one of the E2E test templates in `avm\res\azure-stack-hci\cluster\tests\e2e`. NOTE: these templates all deploy to 'southeastasia' - to use another location, modify the `enforcedLocation` variable.

+## 0.5.4
+
+### Changes
+
+- Updated `Microsoft.Network/networkSecurityGroups` API version from `2025-05-01` to `2025-09-01`
+- Updated the telemetry deployment (`Microsoft.Resources/deployments`) API version from `2024-03-01` to `2025-04-01`
+- Telemetry ID prefix is now sourced from the module's `metadata.json`
+- Corrected parameter descriptions, including documenting that `securityRules` replaces all custom rules of the Network Security Group and that `flushConnection` fails in regions where connection flushing is not available
+
+### Breaking Changes
+
+- None
